Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit). Read-only investigation only — no edits, this is pure research for a plan.

I want to open a DRAFT pull request on GitHub for a new feature branch, specifically to trigger this repo's ephemeral per-PR Managed Runtime (MRT) preview environment so a live demo page can be viewed by stakeholders. Need to understand exactly how that preview mechanism works before planning around it.

Investigate and report back:

1. **Read `.github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml` in full.** Report: what event(s) trigger it (`pull_request`, and if so which types — `opened`, `synchronize`, etc.; does it explicitly check or ignore `github.event.pull_request.draft`?), what base branch(es) it applies to (does it require the PR to target `develop` specifically, or does it run for a PR targeting any base?), what the resulting preview URL/hostname pattern looks like (e.g. `pr-<slug>`), and — critically — which SFCC/commerce backend environment that preview build points at (check what `RETAIL_APP_HOME`-equivalent or commerce-api config it uses — is it the `dev` tier's SFCC instance, or something else?). Quote the exact relevant YAML lines, don't paraphrase from memory.

2. **Check `.github/workflows/qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` job and any other workflow that gates on file paths** — I want to know whether a homepage-only change (e.g. `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`) would actually trigger `deploy-preview.yml` and the rest of the PR-time CI (or whether some path-filter would skip it).

3. **Check whether opening the PR as a GitHub "draft" PR changes anything about which workflows run**, specifically for `deploy-preview.yml` and the main `qa.yml` `QA` workflow — GitHub's own `pull_request` event fires for draft PRs by default unless a workflow explicitly filters `if: github.event.pull_request.draft == false`, so check whether any workflow in this repo has that kind of conditional guard that would need a "ready for review" PR instead of a draft.

4. **Confirm the branch-naming and base-branch conventions this repo actually enforces** for a `feature/*` branch, per `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`/`AGENTS.md`'s own branch-rules table (I already know `feature/*` branches from `develop`, but I specifically need to know: is there anything that would break or behave differently if a NEW feature branch is cut from the TIP of an existing, still-open feature branch — i.e. `feature/B` branched off `feature/A` instead of off `develop` directly — rather than from `develop` itself? Check `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`'s "🔴 Branch Target Check" job specifically, since that ran on PR #85 and is the kind of check that might care about this.)

5. **Check `.docs/` for any environment-topology documentation** (e.g. a file resembling `.docs/prd/environments.md` or similar, or check `.claude/rules/tagging.md`'s own "Environment model" section which I already know exists) for what's officially documented about the preview/`pr-<slug>` tier specifically — I want to cross-check the workflow YAML's real behavior against what's documented, and flag if they disagree (this repo has a history of doc/reality drift on environment topology per its own memory notes).

Report as structured findings with exact YAML excerpts and file:line citations — I'm using this to plan a real draft PR and need to know precisely what will and won't get triggered, not a general description of how MRT previews usually work.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init

1	name: Deploy Preview
2	
3	# Ephemeral per-branch MRT preview environments. On every push to a feature/fix
4	# branch, creates (or reuses) a dedicated MRT environment, syncs runtime env vars,
5	# builds, and deploys — giving devs/testers a live URL to review during PR without
6	# waiting for a merge to develop. Companion teardown workflow: teardown-preview.yml.
7	#
8	# Every ephemeral target is prefixed `pr-`, so it can never collide with the fixed
9	# named environments (dev, dev1, test, sit, stg, uat, production).
10	
11	on:
12	  push:
13	    branches:
14	      - 'feature/**'
15	      - 'fix/**'
16	      - '!fix/release-*'
17	      # `*` doesn't match `/` in GitHub Actions branch globs, so the pattern
18	      # above alone wouldn't exclude a nested fix/release/<version> naming slip
19	      # — this repo's documented convention is the hyphenated
20	      # fix/release-{version}-* form, but this guards defensively either way.
21	      - '!fix/release/**'
22	
23	# Keyed on the raw branch name (not the derived slug) — concurrency groups are
24	# evaluated before any job/step runs, so the key can't depend on a step output.
25	# cancel-in-progress is deliberately false: a cancelled Actions run does NOT cancel
26	# an already-submitted MRT-side operation (a POST/PATCH, or an in-flight
27	# `pwa-kit-dev push`), so a naively-cancelled run's server-side effects could still
28	# land after its successor starts. Same reasoning deploy-test.yml documents for its
29	# own cancel-in-progress: false.
30	concurrency:
31	  group: mrt-preview-${{ github.ref_name }}
32	  cancel-in-progress: false
33	
34	permissions:
35	  contents: read
36	  pull-requests: write
37	
38	jobs:
39	  deploy-preview:
40	    name: Deploy Preview
41	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
42	    # Deliberately NOT bound to a GitHub Environment. It used to declare
43	    # `environment: dev`, which made GitHub log a real Deployment tagged
44	    # "dev" on every single push to a feature/fix branch -- every PR showed
45	    # a misleading "Deployed to dev" even though the actual target is
46	    # always an isolated pr-<slug> MRT preview, never the shared dev tier
47	    # (confirmed against real Deployment records, 2026-08-25). The binding
48	    # wasn't doing anything functional either: MRT_USER/MRT_API_KEY below
49	    # are already repo-level secrets, the dev-tier Variables this job
50	    # actually needs are fetched explicitly via the GitHub API further down
51	    # (SOURCE_ENV: dev, using GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN) rather than the native
52	    # environment: binding, and `dev` carries no protection rules to lose.
53	    # 12 min target-wait deadline + headroom for npm install/build/push — a
54	    # tighter timeout could cancel the job mid-wait, and a cancelled Actions run
55	    # does not cancel an already-submitted MRT-side operation (see the
56	    # concurrency note above), so the timeout needs real margin over the wait
57	    # budget, not just the wait budget itself.
58	    timeout-minutes: 35
59	    env:
60	      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
61	      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
62	      MRT_PROJECT: zimmermann
63	    steps:
64	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
65	
66	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
67	        with:
68	          node-version: '24'
69	          cache: 'npm'
70	
71	      - name: Install dependencies
72	        run: npm install --include=dev
73	
74	      - name: Compute MRT preview slug
75	        id: slug
76	        env:
77	          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
78	        run: |
79	          SLUG=$(node scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs "$BRANCH_NAME")
80	          echo "slug=$SLUG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
81	
82	      - name: Read desired proxy config from config/dev.js
83	        id: proxy
84	        run: |
85	          PROXY_JSON=$(node -e "
86	            const cfgs = require('./config/dev.js')?.ssrParameters?.proxyConfigs
87	            if (!Array.isArray(cfgs) || cfgs.length === 0) {
88	              console.error('config/dev.js has no ssrParameters.proxyConfigs')
89	              process.exit(1)
90	            }
91	            console.log(JSON.stringify(cfgs))
92	          ")
93	          echo "json=$PROXY_JSON" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
94	
95	      # Region and proxy config are NOT derived from the bundle push — confirmed
96	      # live this session: two successful `pwa-kit-dev push` calls left
97	      # ssr_proxy_configs null on a freshly created target, and region defaults to
98	      # us-east-2 unless set explicitly. Both must be set here, explicitly, and
99	      # self-healed on every run in case a target was ever created out-of-band
100	      # (e.g. by hand through the MRT console) with the wrong values.
101	      - name: Ensure MRT target exists with correct region/proxy config
102	        id: ensure
103	        env:
104	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
105	          PROXY_JSON: ${{ steps.proxy.outputs.json }}
106	        run: |
107	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
108	          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
109	
110	          SLUG, PROJECT = os.environ['SLUG'], os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
111	          USER, API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_USER'], os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
112	          DESIRED_PROXY = json.loads(os.environ['PROXY_JSON'])
113	          DESIRED_REGION = 'ap-southeast-2'
114	
115	          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
116	          headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {token}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
117	          base = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/'
118	
119	          def get_target():
120	              req = urllib.request.Request(base + f'target/{SLUG}/', headers=headers)
121	              for attempt in range(3):
122	                  try:
123	                      return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
124	                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
125	                      if e.code == 404:
126	                          return None
127	                      if attempt < 2 and (e.code == 429 or e.code >= 500):
128	                          print(f'Transient HTTP {e.code} on target lookup — backing off 30s')
129	                          time.sleep(30)
130	                          continue
131	                      raise
132	                  except urllib.error.URLError as e:
133	                      if attempt < 2:
134	                          print(f'Connection error on target lookup ({e.reason}) — backing off 30s')
135	                          time.sleep(30)
136	                          continue
137	                      raise
138	
139	          def proxy_matches(existing_proxy):
140	              if not existing_proxy:
141	                  return False
142	              # Compare the full config per entry, not just path/host — a field
143	              # this repo doesn't use today drifting silently would otherwise
144	              # never trigger the self-heal PATCH below.
145	              norm = lambda cfgs: sorted(json.dumps(c, sort_keys=True) for c in cfgs)
146	              return norm(existing_proxy) == norm(DESIRED_PROXY)
147	
148	          existing = get_target()
149	          if existing is None:
150	              print(f'No existing target for {SLUG} — creating in {DESIRED_REGION}.')
151	              payload = {
152	                  'name': SLUG,
153	                  'ssr_region': DESIRED_REGION,
154	                  'ssr_proxy_configs': DESIRED_PROXY,
155	              }
156	              req = urllib.request.Request(
157	                  base + 'target/', data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method='POST', headers=headers
158	              )
159	              try:
160	                  resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
161	                  print(f'Create requested: {resp.status}')
162	              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
163	                  print(f'Create failed {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
164	                  sys.exit(1)
165	          else:
166	              print(f'Target {SLUG} already exists (state={existing.get("state")}) — reusing.')
167	              needs_patch = (
168	                  existing.get('ssr_region') != DESIRED_REGION
169	                  or not proxy_matches(existing.get('ssr_proxy_configs'))
170	              )
171	              if needs_patch:
172	                  print(f'Target {SLUG} has drifted region/proxy config — self-healing.')
173	                  payload = {'ssr_region': DESIRED_REGION, 'ssr_proxy_configs': DESIRED_PROXY}
174	                  req = urllib.request.Request(
175	                      base + f'target/{SLUG}/', data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method='PATCH', headers=headers
176	                  )
177	                  try:
178	                      urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
179	                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
180	                      print(f'Region/proxy patch failed {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
181	                      sys.exit(1)
182	                  # The PATCH alone updates target config but not the already-running
183	                  # Lambda — confirmed live, the relocation only takes effect after the
184	                  # next `pwa-kit-dev push`, which always runs later in this job.
185	          PYEOF
186	
187	      - name: Wait for target to reach ACTIVE
188	        id: wait
189	        env:
190	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
191	        run: |
192	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
193	          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
194	
195	          SLUG, PROJECT = os.environ['SLUG'], os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
196	          USER, API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_USER'], os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
197	          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
198	          headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {token}'}
199	          url = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{SLUG}/'
200	
201	          # Fresh create ~5 min, region-relocation redeploy ~2 min, per validated
202	          # session data — poll generously but bounded so a stuck target fails loudly.
203	          deadline, poll_every = time.time() + 12 * 60, 20
204	          while True:
205	              req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
206	              try:
207	                  body = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
208	              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
209	                  if e.code == 429:
210	                      if time.time() > deadline:
211	                          print('Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (persistently rate limited)', file=sys.stderr)
212	                          sys.exit(1)
213	                      try:
214	                          backoff = max(1, min(60, int(e.headers.get('Retry-After', 30))))
215	                      except (TypeError, ValueError):
216	                          backoff = 30
217	                      print(f'Rate limited — backing off {backoff}s')
218	                      time.sleep(backoff)
219	                      continue
220	                  # The create request is asynchronous — a freshly-created target
221	                  # can briefly 404 (not yet visible) or 5xx before settling, not
222	                  # just while waiting on state transitions. Retry those like any
223	                  # other not-yet-ready signal instead of failing the job outright.
224	                  if e.code == 404 or e.code >= 500:
225	                      print(f'Transient HTTP {e.code} — target not visible yet, retrying')
226	                      if time.time() > deadline:
227	                          print(f'Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (last error={e.code})', file=sys.stderr)
228	                          sys.exit(1)
229	                      time.sleep(poll_every)
230	                      continue
231	                  raise
232	              except urllib.error.URLError as e:
233	                  print(f'Connection error ({e.reason}) — retrying')
234	                  if time.time() > deadline:
235	                      print('Timed out waiting for ACTIVE', file=sys.stderr)
236	                      sys.exit(1)
237	                  time.sleep(poll_every)
238	                  continue
239	              state = body.get('state')
240	              print(f'target {SLUG} state={state}')
241	              if state == 'ACTIVE':
242	                  # Read the real hostname from the API rather than assuming a
243	                  # fixed host suffix — that suffix is MRT-account-specific and
244	                  # could change; a hardcoded guess would silently publish a dead
245	                  # URL in the PR comment if it ever did.
246	                  hostname = body.get('ssr_external_hostname')
247	                  if not hostname:
248	                      print('Target is ACTIVE but ssr_external_hostname is empty', file=sys.stderr)
249	                      sys.exit(1)
250	                  with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
251	                      out.write(f'hostname={hostname}\n')
252	                  break
253	              if state and state.endswith('_FAILED'):
254	                  print(f'Target entered failed state: {state}', file=sys.stderr)
255	                  sys.exit(1)
256	              if time.time() > deadline:
257	                  print(f'Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (last state={state})', file=sys.stderr)
258	                  sys.exit(1)
259	              time.sleep(poll_every)
260	          PYEOF
261	
262	      # Steps below lift .github/workflows/sync-env-vars-to-mrt.yml's env-var-sync
263	      # logic near-verbatim. The one structural change: source (which GitHub
264	      # Environment to read from) and destination (which MRT target to PATCH) are
265	      # no longer the same value — source is always `dev`+`shared` regardless of
266	      # branch, since there's no per-branch GitHub Environment; destination is the
267	      # computed slug.
268	      - name: Parse syncable keys from .env.sample
269	        id: parse
270	        run: |
271	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
272	          import re, os, json
273	
274	          # Only keys explicitly tagged `# mrt:true` in .env.sample are synced.
275	          keys = []
276	          pending_mrt = False
277	          with open('.env.sample') as f:
278	              for line in f:
279	                  line = line.rstrip('\n')
280	                  if re.match(r'^#\s*mrt:true', line):
281	                      pending_mrt = True
282	                      continue
283	                  stripped = line.strip()
284	                  if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
285	                      if not stripped:
286	                          pending_mrt = False
287	                      continue
288	                  eq = stripped.find('=')
289	                  if eq == -1:
290	                      pending_mrt = False
291	                      continue
292	                  key = stripped[:eq].strip()
293	                  if pending_mrt:
294	                      keys.append(key)
295	                  pending_mrt = False
296	
297	          print(f'Parsed {len(keys)} MRT-tagged keys from .env.sample')
298	          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
299	              out.write(f'keys={json.dumps(keys)}\n')
300	          PYEOF
301	
302	      - name: Fetch GitHub Environment variables (dev + shared)
303	        id: gh_vars
304	        env:
305	          # Always dev — ephemeral preview branches have no GitHub Environment of
306	          # their own to source from.
307	          SOURCE_ENV: dev
308	          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
309	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN }}
310	        run: |
311	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
312	          import json, os, subprocess, sys
313	
314	          SOURCE_ENV = os.environ['SOURCE_ENV']
315	          REPO = os.environ['REPO']
316	
317	          def fetch_env(env_name):
318	              """Fetch all variables from a GitHub Environment. Returns dict of name→value."""
319	              import urllib.parse
320	              safe_name = urllib.parse.quote(env_name, safe='')
321	              result = subprocess.run(
322	                  ['gh', 'api', f'/repos/{REPO}/environments/{safe_name}/variables',
323	                   '--paginate', '--jq', '.variables[] | {(.name): .value}'],
324	                  capture_output=True, text=True
325	              )
326	              if result.returncode != 0:
327	                  print(f'GitHub API error fetching {env_name}: {result.stderr}', file=sys.stderr)
328	                  sys.exit(1)
329	              out = {}
330	              for line in result.stdout.strip().splitlines():
331	                  if line:
332	                      out.update(json.loads(line))
333	              return out
334	
335	          shared_vars = fetch_env('shared')
336	          target_vars = fetch_env(SOURCE_ENV)
337	          all_vars = dict(shared_vars)
338	          for name, value in target_vars.items():
339	              if value or name not in all_vars:
340	                  all_vars[name] = value
341	
342	          print(f'Found {len(shared_vars)} variables in GitHub Environment: shared')
343	          print(f'Found {len(target_vars)} variables in GitHub Environment: {SOURCE_ENV}')
344	          print(f'Merged total (target overrides shared): {len(all_vars)}')
345	
346	          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
347	              out.write(f'vars={json.dumps(all_vars)}\n')
348	          PYEOF
349	
350	      - name: Sync env vars to the preview target
351	        env:
352	          MRT_TARGET_SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
353	          SYNC_KEYS: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.keys }}
354	          GH_VARS: ${{ steps.gh_vars.outputs.vars }}
355	        run: |
356	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
357	          import base64, json, os, sys, urllib.request, urllib.error
358	
359	          TARGET  = os.environ['MRT_TARGET_SLUG']
360	          PROJECT = os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
361	          USER    = os.environ['MRT_USER']
362	          API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
363	
364	          syncable_keys = json.loads(os.environ['SYNC_KEYS'])
365	          gh_vars       = json.loads(os.environ['GH_VARS'])
366	
367	          payload = {}
368	          skipped_empty = []
369	          skipped_missing = []
370	          for key in syncable_keys:
371	              if key in gh_vars:
372	                  val = gh_vars[key]
373	                  if val:
374	                      payload[key] = {'value': val}
375	                  else:
376	                      skipped_empty.append(key)
377	              else:
378	                  skipped_missing.append(key)
379	
380	          print(f'Keys to sync:    {len(payload)}')
381	          print(f'Skipped (empty): {len(skipped_empty)}')
382	          print(f'Skipped (not in GitHub Environment): {len(skipped_missing)}')
383	
384	          if not payload:
385	              print('Nothing to sync.')
386	              sys.exit(0)
387	
388	          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
389	          url   = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{TARGET}/env-var/'
390	          req   = urllib.request.Request(
391	              url,
392	              data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
393	              method='PATCH',
394	              headers={
395	                  'Authorization': f'Basic {token}',
396	                  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
397	              },
398	          )
399	          try:
400	              resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
401	              print(f'\nMRT response: {resp.status} {resp.reason}')
402	              print(f'Synced {len(payload)} env vars to MRT target: {TARGET}')
403	          except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
404	              print(f'MRT API error {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
405	              sys.exit(1)
406	          except urllib.error.URLError as e:
407	              print(f'MRT API connection error: {e.reason}', file=sys.stderr)
408	              sys.exit(1)
409	          PYEOF
410	
411	      # Must run after env vars are synced, not before — a target with no env
412	      # vars 500s on every request (confirmed live).
413	      - name: Build and push to preview target
414	        env:
415	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
416	        run: |
417	          npm run build
418	          npx pwa-kit-dev push -t "$SLUG" -w
419	
420	      # Deliberately placed after the push above, not right after the "wait
421	      # for ACTIVE" step that first produced steps.wait.outputs.hostname --
422	      # the target existing and being ACTIVE only means the MRT
423	      # infrastructure is ready, not that this PR's own code is live there
424	      # yet. e2e-browserstack (qa.yml) downloads this artifact and points
425	      # BrowserStack at the resulting URL instead of the static test-tier
426	      # RETAIL_APP_HOME, so it actually tests this PR's own changes rather
427	      # than whatever unrelated build happens to be live on test tier
428	      # (test is a deliberate, tag-promoted environment with no guaranteed
429	      # relationship to any given PR -- confirmed with the developer,
430	      # 2026-08-25). Short retention: only needed within this PR's own CI
431	      # cycle, never referenced again after.
432	      - name: Persist preview hostname for e2e-browserstack
433	        env:
434	          PREVIEW_HOSTNAME: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.hostname }}
435	        run: printf '%s\n' "$PREVIEW_HOSTNAME" > preview-hostname.txt
436	
437	      - name: Upload preview hostname artifact
438	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
439	        with:
440	          name: mrt-preview-hostname
441	          path: preview-hostname.txt
442	          retention-days: 1
443	
444	      - name: Find open PR for this branch
445	        id: pr
446	        env:
447	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
448	          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
449	        run: |
450	          NUMBER=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
451	          echo "number=$NUMBER" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
452	
453	      # Upserts on an exact HTML-comment marker (not a text substring) so a
454	      # coincidental match in someone else's comment can't be mistaken for ours,
455	      # and so redeploys update the same comment instead of spamming the thread —
456	      # the URL is deterministic from the slug and never changes between pushes.
457	      # Pattern mirrors protected-file-guard.yml's Tier 2 warning comment.
458	      - name: Post or update preview URL comment
459	        if: steps.pr.outputs.number != ''
460	        uses: actions/github-script@v7
461	        env:
462	          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.number }}
463	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
464	          PREVIEW_HOSTNAME: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.hostname }}
465	        with:
466	          script: |
467	            const prNumber = Number(process.env.PR_NUMBER)
468	            const marker = `<!-- mrt-preview:${process.env.SLUG} -->`
469	            const previewUrl = `https://${process.env.PREVIEW_HOSTNAME}`
470	            const body = `${marker}\n## 🚀 MRT Preview Environment\n\n**Live preview:** ${previewUrl}\n\nTarget: \`${process.env.SLUG}\` · Updated: ${new Date().toISOString()}\n\n_Auto-updated on every push to this branch. Torn down when this PR closes or the branch is deleted._`
471	
472	            // Paginated — listComments only returns the first page (30) by
473	            // default, which would miss the marker on a busy PR and start
474	            // duplicating comments instead of updating in place. c.body is
475	            // optional in the REST payload, so guard against null too.
476	            const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments, {
477	              owner: context.repo.owner,
478	              repo: context.repo.repo,
479	              issue_number: prNumber,
480	              per_page: 100,
481	            })
482	            const existing = comments.find(
483	              (c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(marker) && c.user?.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
484	            )
485	            if (existing) {
486	              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
487	                owner: context.repo.owner,
488	                repo: context.repo.repo,
489	                comment_id: existing.id,
490	                body,
491	              })
492	            } else {
493	              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
494	                owner: context.repo.owner,
495	                repo: context.repo.repo,
496	                issue_number: prNumber,
497	                body,
498	              })
499	            }

file.content:
name: Deploy Preview

# Ephemeral per-branch MRT preview environments. On every push to a feature/fix
# branch, creates (or reuses) a dedicated MRT environment, syncs runtime env vars,
# builds, and deploys — giving devs/testers a live URL to review during PR without
# waiting for a merge to develop. Companion teardown workflow: teardown-preview.yml.
#
# Every ephemeral target is prefixed `pr-`, so it can never collide with the fixed
# named environments (dev, dev1, test, sit, stg, uat, production).

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'feature/**'
      - 'fix/**'
      - '!fix/release-*'
      # `*` doesn't match `/` in GitHub Actions branch globs, so the pattern
      # above alone wouldn't exclude a nested fix/release/<version> naming slip
      # — this repo's documented convention is the hyphenated
      # fix/release-{version}-* form, but this guards defensively either way.
      - '!fix/release/**'

# Keyed on the raw branch name (not the derived slug) — concurrency groups are
# evaluated before any job/step runs, so the key can't depend on a step output.
# cancel-in-progress is deliberately false: a cancelled Actions run does NOT cancel
# an already-submitted MRT-side operation (a POST/PATCH, or an in-flight
# `pwa-kit-dev push`), so a naively-cancelled run's server-side effects could still
# land after its successor starts. Same reasoning deploy-test.yml documents for its
# own cancel-in-progress: false.
concurrency:
  group: mrt-preview-${{ github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  deploy-preview:
    name: Deploy Preview
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Deliberately NOT bound to a GitHub Environment. It used to declare
    # `environment: dev`, which made GitHub log a real Deployment tagged
    # "dev" on every single push to a feature/fix branch -- every PR showed
    # a misleading "Deployed to dev" even though the actual target is
    # always an isolated pr-<slug> MRT preview, never the shared dev tier
    # (confirmed against real Deployment records, 2026-08-25). The binding
    # wasn't doing anything functional either: MRT_USER/MRT_API_KEY below
    # are already repo-level secrets, the dev-tier Variables this job
    # actually needs are fetched explicitly via the GitHub API further down
    # (SOURCE_ENV: dev, using GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN) rather than the native
    # environment: binding, and `dev` carries no protection rules to lose.
    # 12 min target-wait deadline + headroom for npm install/build/push — a
    # tighter timeout could cancel the job mid-wait, and a cancelled Actions run
    # does not cancel an already-submitted MRT-side operation (see the
    # concurrency note above), so the timeout needs real margin over the wait
    # budget, not just the wait budget itself.
    timeout-minutes: 35
    env:
      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
      MRT_PROJECT: zimmermann
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Compute MRT preview slug
        id: slug
        env:
          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          SLUG=$(node scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs "$BRANCH_NAME")
          echo "slug=$SLUG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Read desired proxy config from config/dev.js
        id: proxy
        run: |
          PROXY_JSON=$(node -e "
            const cfgs = require('./config/dev.js')?.ssrParameters?.proxyConfigs
            if (!Array.isArray(cfgs) || cfgs.length === 0) {
              console.error('config/dev.js has no ssrParameters.proxyConfigs')
              process.exit(1)
            }
            console.log(JSON.stringify(cfgs))
          ")
          echo "json=$PROXY_JSON" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Region and proxy config are NOT derived from the bundle push — confirmed
      # live this session: two successful `pwa-kit-dev push` calls left
      # ssr_proxy_configs null on a freshly created target, and region defaults to
      # us-east-2 unless set explicitly. Both must be set here, explicitly, and
      # self-healed on every run in case a target was ever created out-of-band
      # (e.g. by hand through the MRT console) with the wrong values.
      - name: Ensure MRT target exists with correct region/proxy config
        id: ensure
        env:
          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
          PROXY_JSON: ${{ steps.proxy.outputs.json }}
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error

          SLUG, PROJECT = os.environ['SLUG'], os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
          USER, API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_USER'], os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
          DESIRED_PROXY = json.loads(os.environ['PROXY_JSON'])
          DESIRED_REGION = 'ap-southeast-2'

          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
          headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {token}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
          base = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/'

          def get_target():
              req = urllib.request.Request(base + f'target/{SLUG}/', headers=headers)
              for attempt in range(3):
                  try:
                      return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
                      if e.code == 404:
                          return None
                      if attempt < 2 and (e.code == 429 or e.code >= 500):
                          print(f'Transient HTTP {e.code} on target lookup — backing off 30s')
                          time.sleep(30)
                          continue
                      raise
                  except urllib.error.URLError as e:
                      if attempt < 2:
                          print(f'Connection error on target lookup ({e.reason}) — backing off 30s')
                          time.sleep(30)
                          continue
                      raise

          def proxy_matches(existing_proxy):
              if not existing_proxy:
                  return False
              # Compare the full config per entry, not just path/host — a field
              # this repo doesn't use today drifting silently would otherwise
              # never trigger the self-heal PATCH below.
              norm = lambda cfgs: sorted(json.dumps(c, sort_keys=True) for c in cfgs)
              return norm(existing_proxy) == norm(DESIRED_PROXY)

          existing = get_target()
          if existing is None:
              print(f'No existing target for {SLUG} — creating in {DESIRED_REGION}.')
              payload = {
                  'name': SLUG,
                  'ssr_region': DESIRED_REGION,
                  'ssr_proxy_configs': DESIRED_PROXY,
              }
              req = urllib.request.Request(
                  base + 'target/', data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method='POST', headers=headers
              )
              try:
                  resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
                  print(f'Create requested: {resp.status}')
              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
                  print(f'Create failed {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
                  sys.exit(1)
          else:
              print(f'Target {SLUG} already exists (state={existing.get("state")}) — reusing.')
              needs_patch = (
                  existing.get('ssr_region') != DESIRED_REGION
                  or not proxy_matches(existing.get('ssr_proxy_configs'))
              )
              if needs_patch:
                  print(f'Target {SLUG} has drifted region/proxy config — self-healing.')
                  payload = {'ssr_region': DESIRED_REGION, 'ssr_proxy_configs': DESIRED_PROXY}
                  req = urllib.request.Request(
                      base + f'target/{SLUG}/', data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method='PATCH', headers=headers
                  )
                  try:
                      urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
                      print(f'Region/proxy patch failed {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
                      sys.exit(1)
                  # The PATCH alone updates target config but not the already-running
                  # Lambda — confirmed live, the relocation only takes effect after the
                  # next `pwa-kit-dev push`, which always runs later in this job.
          PYEOF

      - name: Wait for target to reach ACTIVE
        id: wait
        env:
          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error

          SLUG, PROJECT = os.environ['SLUG'], os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
          USER, API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_USER'], os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
          headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {token}'}
          url = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{SLUG}/'

          # Fresh create ~5 min, region-relocation redeploy ~2 min, per validated
          # session data — poll generously but bounded so a stuck target fails loudly.
          deadline, poll_every = time.time() + 12 * 60, 20
          while True:
              req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
              try:
                  body = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
                  if e.code == 429:
                      if time.time() > deadline:
                          print('Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (persistently rate limited)', file=sys.stderr)
                          sys.exit(1)
                      try:
                          backoff = max(1, min(60, int(e.headers.get('Retry-After', 30))))
                      except (TypeError, ValueError):
                          backoff = 30
                      print(f'Rate limited — backing off {backoff}s')
                      time.sleep(backoff)
                      continue
                  # The create request is asynchronous — a freshly-created target
                  # can briefly 404 (not yet visible) or 5xx before settling, not
                  # just while waiting on state transitions. Retry those like any
                  # other not-yet-ready signal instead of failing the job outright.
                  if e.code == 404 or e.code >= 500:
                      print(f'Transient HTTP {e.code} — target not visible yet, retrying')
                      if time.time() > deadline:
                          print(f'Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (last error={e.code})', file=sys.stderr)
                          sys.exit(1)
                      time.sleep(poll_every)
                      continue
                  raise
              except urllib.error.URLError as e:
                  print(f'Connection error ({e.reason}) — retrying')
                  if time.time() > deadline:
                      print('Timed out waiting for ACTIVE', file=sys.stderr)
                      sys.exit(1)
                  time.sleep(poll_every)
                  continue
              state = body.get('state')
              print(f'target {SLUG} state={state}')
              if state == 'ACTIVE':
                  # Read the real hostname from the API rather than assuming a
                  # fixed host suffix — that suffix is MRT-account-specific and
                  # could change; a hardcoded guess would silently publish a dead
                  # URL in the PR comment if it ever did.
                  hostname = body.get('ssr_external_hostname')
                  if not hostname:
                      print('Target is ACTIVE but ssr_external_hostname is empty', file=sys.stderr)
                      sys.exit(1)
                  with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
                      out.write(f'hostname={hostname}\n')
                  break
              if state and state.endswith('_FAILED'):
                  print(f'Target entered failed state: {state}', file=sys.stderr)
                  sys.exit(1)
              if time.time() > deadline:
                  print(f'Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (last state={state})', file=sys.stderr)
                  sys.exit(1)
              time.sleep(poll_every)
          PYEOF

      # Steps below lift .github/workflows/sync-env-vars-to-mrt.yml's env-var-sync
      # logic near-verbatim. The one structural change: source (which GitHub
      # Environment to read from) and destination (which MRT target to PATCH) are
      # no longer the same value — source is always `dev`+`shared` regardless of
      # branch, since there's no per-branch GitHub Environment; destination is the
      # computed slug.
      - name: Parse syncable keys from .env.sample
        id: parse
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
          import re, os, json

          # Only keys explicitly tagged `# mrt:true` in .env.sample are synced.
          keys = []
          pending_mrt = False
          with open('.env.sample') as f:
              for line in f:
                  line = line.rstrip('\n')
                  if re.match(r'^#\s*mrt:true', line):
                      pending_mrt = True
                      continue
                  stripped = line.strip()
                  if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
                      if not stripped:
                          pending_mrt = False
                      continue
                  eq = stripped.find('=')
                  if eq == -1:
                      pending_mrt = False
                      continue
                  key = stripped[:eq].strip()
                  if pending_mrt:
                      keys.append(key)
                  pending_mrt = False

          print(f'Parsed {len(keys)} MRT-tagged keys from .env.sample')
          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
              out.write(f'keys={json.dumps(keys)}\n')
          PYEOF

      - name: Fetch GitHub Environment variables (dev + shared)
        id: gh_vars
        env:
          # Always dev — ephemeral preview branches have no GitHub Environment of
          # their own to source from.
          SOURCE_ENV: dev
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
          import json, os, subprocess, sys

          SOURCE_ENV = os.environ['SOURCE_ENV']
          REPO = os.environ['REPO']

          def fetch_env(env_name):
              """Fetch all variables from a GitHub Environment. Returns dict of name→value."""
              import urllib.parse
              safe_name = urllib.parse.quote(env_name, safe='')
              result = subprocess.run(
                  ['gh', 'api', f'/repos/{REPO}/environments/{safe_name}/variables',
                   '--paginate', '--jq', '.variables[] | {(.name): .value}'],
                  capture_output=True, text=True
              )
              if result.returncode != 0:
                  print(f'GitHub API error fetching {env_name}: {result.stderr}', file=sys.stderr)
                  sys.exit(1)
              out = {}
              for line in result.stdout.strip().splitlines():
                  if line:
                      out.update(json.loads(line))
              return out

          shared_vars = fetch_env('shared')
          target_vars = fetch_env(SOURCE_ENV)
          all_vars = dict(shared_vars)
          for name, value in target_vars.items():
              if value or name not in all_vars:
                  all_vars[name] = value

          print(f'Found {len(shared_vars)} variables in GitHub Environment: shared')
          print(f'Found {len(target_vars)} variables in GitHub Environment: {SOURCE_ENV}')
          print(f'Merged total (target overrides shared): {len(all_vars)}')

          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
              out.write(f'vars={json.dumps(all_vars)}\n')
          PYEOF

      - name: Sync env vars to the preview target
        env:
          MRT_TARGET_SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
          SYNC_KEYS: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.keys }}
          GH_VARS: ${{ steps.gh_vars.outputs.vars }}
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
          import base64, json, os, sys, urllib.request, urllib.error

          TARGET  = os.environ['MRT_TARGET_SLUG']
          PROJECT = os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
          USER    = os.environ['MRT_USER']
          API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']

          syncable_keys = json.loads(os.environ['SYNC_KEYS'])
          gh_vars       = json.loads(os.environ['GH_VARS'])

          payload = {}
          skipped_empty = []
          skipped_missing = []
          for key in syncable_keys:
              if key in gh_vars:
                  val = gh_vars[key]
                  if val:
                      payload[key] = {'value': val}
                  else:
                      skipped_empty.append(key)
              else:
                  skipped_missing.append(key)

          print(f'Keys to sync:    {len(payload)}')
          print(f'Skipped (empty): {len(skipped_empty)}')
          print(f'Skipped (not in GitHub Environment): {len(skipped_missing)}')

          if not payload:
              print('Nothing to sync.')
              sys.exit(0)

          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
          url   = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{TARGET}/env-var/'
          req   = urllib.request.Request(
              url,
              data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
              method='PATCH',
              headers={
                  'Authorization': f'Basic {token}',
                  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
              },
          )
          try:
              resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
              print(f'\nMRT response: {resp.status} {resp.reason}')
              print(f'Synced {len(payload)} env vars to MRT target: {TARGET}')
          except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
              print(f'MRT API error {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
              sys.exit(1)
          except urllib.error.URLError as e:
              print(f'MRT API connection error: {e.reason}', file=sys.stderr)
              sys.exit(1)
          PYEOF

      # Must run after env vars are synced, not before — a target with no env
      # vars 500s on every request (confirmed live).
      - name: Build and push to preview target
        env:
          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
        run: |
          npm run build
          npx pwa-kit-dev push -t "$SLUG" -w

      # Deliberately placed after the push above, not right after the "wait
      # for ACTIVE" step that first produced steps.wait.outputs.hostname --
      # the target existing and being ACTIVE only means the MRT
      # infrastructure is ready, not that this PR's own code is live there
      # yet. e2e-browserstack (qa.yml) downloads this artifact and points
      # BrowserStack at the resulting URL instead of the static test-tier
      # RETAIL_APP_HOME, so it actually tests this PR's own changes rather
      # than whatever unrelated build happens to be live on test tier
      # (test is a deliberate, tag-promoted environment with no guaranteed
      # relationship to any given PR -- confirmed with the developer,
      # 2026-08-25). Short retention: only needed within this PR's own CI
      # cycle, never referenced again after.
      - name: Persist preview hostname for e2e-browserstack
        env:
          PREVIEW_HOSTNAME: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.hostname }}
        run: printf '%s\n' "$PREVIEW_HOSTNAME" > preview-hostname.txt

      - name: Upload preview hostname artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: mrt-preview-hostname
          path: preview-hostname.txt
          retention-days: 1

      - name: Find open PR for this branch
        id: pr
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          NUMBER=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          echo "number=$NUMBER" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Upserts on an exact HTML-comment marker (not a text substring) so a
      # coincidental match in someone else's comment can't be mistaken for ours,
      # and so redeploys update the same comment instead of spamming the thread —
      # the URL is deterministic from the slug and never changes between pushes.
      # Pattern mirrors protected-file-guard.yml's Tier 2 warning comment.
      - name: Post or update preview URL comment
        if: steps.pr.outputs.number != ''
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.number }}
          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
          PREVIEW_HOSTNAME: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.hostname }}
        with:
          script: |
            const prNumber = Number(process.env.PR_NUMBER)
            const marker = `<!-- mrt-preview:${process.env.SLUG} -->`
            const previewUrl = `https://${process.env.PREVIEW_HOSTNAME}`
            const body = `${marker}\n## 🚀 MRT Preview Environment\n\n**Live preview:** ${previewUrl}\n\nTarget: \`${process.env.SLUG}\` · Updated: ${new Date().toISOString()}\n\n_Auto-updated on every push to this branch. Torn down when this PR closes or the branch is deleted._`

            // Paginated — listComments only returns the first page (30) by
            // default, which would miss the marker on a busy PR and start
            // duplicating comments instead of updating in place. c.body is
            // optional in the REST payload, so guard against null too.
            const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments, {
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: prNumber,
              per_page: 100,
            })
            const existing = comments.find(
              (c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(marker) && c.user?.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
            )
            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              })
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: prNumber,
                body,
              })
            }

64	        id: changed
65	        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
66	        with:
67	          # Diff against the previous push on this PR branch, not the PR's
68	          # merge-base with develop/release. Without this, once ANY commit in
69	          # the PR's history touches a relevant path (e.g. config/**), every
70	          # later push re-triggers Storybook/E2E for the rest of the PR's
71	          # life — including a docs-only follow-up commit — because the
72	          # cumulative base...head diff still contains that earlier change.
73	          # Safe for required-status-check semantics: GitHub gates merge on
74	          # the latest SHA's checks, and a "skipped" job counts as passing
75	          # (see the always()/skipped handling on e2e-localhost below) — so
76	          # skipping here just means nothing e2e/storybook-relevant changed
77	          # since the last time those suites ran. Does not help across a
78	          # force-push/rebase (no well-defined "previous remote commit" in
79	          # that case) — not this project's normal workflow per AGENTS.md.
80	          since_last_remote_commit: true
81	          # Default separator is a space, which breaks the exact-line match
82	          # ("grep -qxF") "Compute E2E scope" does below against a multi-file
83	          # *_all_changed_files output — a space-joined string only matches
84	          # when there's exactly one file. Newline-joined lets grep -x match
85	          # each changed file independently regardless of how many there are.
86	          separator: "\n"
87	          files_yaml: |
88	            storybook:
89	              - 'overrides/app/components/**'
90	              - 'overrides/app/pages/**'
91	              - 'overrides/app/hooks/**'
92	              - 'overrides/app/theme/**'
93	              - 'overrides/app/types/**'
94	              - '.storybook/**'
95	              - 'package.json'
96	              - 'package-lock.json'
97	            e2e:
98	              - 'overrides/**'
99	              - 'e2e/**'
100	              - 'config/**'
101	              - 'worker/**'
102	              - 'mobify.config.js'
103	              - 'playwright.config.*'
104	              - '.github/workflows/qa.yml'
105	              - '.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml'
106	              - 'browserstack.yml'
107	              - 'scripts/computeBuildName.mjs'
108	            e2e_homepage:
109	              - 'overrides/app/pages/home/**'
110	              - 'overrides/app/components/header/**'
111	              - 'e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/**'
112	              - 'e2e/features/homepage/**'
113	              - 'e2e/support/pages/HomePage.js'

121	      # Resolve e2e_scope to "full", a single area name (e.g. "homepage")
122	      # consumed by e2e-localhost's --grep filter, or "skip". Defaults to
123	      # "full" on release/** (unchanged — a release PR aggregates a whole
124	      # sprint and gets the supervised, thorough pre-merge treatment per
125	      # releaseBranchesRules.md). On a develop-targeted PR, anything that
126	      # can't be narrowed to one area now resolves to "skip" instead of
127	      # "full" (changed 2026-08-25, at the developer's request) --
128	      # e2e-localhost no longer runs the entire suite on every PR whose
129	      # diff touches a shared/global path or an unclaimed area; that
130	      # broader regression coverage is deferred to the existing post-merge
131	      # P0 gates instead (deploy-test.yml's gate, digital-sit.yml's
132	      # playwright-p0 on release/**). Deliberate trade-off: a develop PR
133	      # that can't be scoped gets no PR-time E2E run at all now, only
134	      # unit tests / Storybook / BrowserStack (if a Jira key matches) —
135	      # full/non-P0 regressions on such a PR are caught later, at Test/SIT
136	      # deploy, not before merge. See testing.md > Change-scoped E2E.
137	      - name: Compute E2E scope
138	        id: scope
139	        # ALL/HOMEPAGE go through env: rather than being interpolated
140	        # directly into the script — a changed_files output is built from
141	        # real filenames in the diff, and interpolating one straight into
142	        # `run:` would let a filename containing quotes/shell syntax break
143	        # out of the assignment and execute on the runner (zizmor:
144	        # template-injection). Reading from env avoids that entirely.
145	        env:
146	          ALL: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_all_changed_files }}
147	          HOMEPAGE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_homepage_all_changed_files }}
148	        run: |
149	          if [[ "${{ github.base_ref }}" == release/* ]]; then
150	            echo "e2e_scope=full" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
151	            exit 0
152	          fi
153	
154	          if [[ -z "$ALL" ]]; then
155	            echo "e2e_scope=skip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
156	            exit 0
157	          fi
158	
159	          # Narrow to "homepage" only if every e2e-relevant changed file is
160	          # also in the homepage allow-list — a single file outside it (a
161	          # shared/global path, or one no area has claimed) skips the
162	          # PR-time run entirely, on purpose (see the step comment above).
163	          SCOPE="homepage"
164	          while IFS= read -r f; do
165	            [[ -z "$f" ]] && continue
166	            if ! grep -qxF "$f" <<< "$HOMEPAGE"; then
167	              SCOPE="skip"
168	              break
169	            fi
170	          done <<< "$ALL"
171	          echo "e2e_scope=$SCOPE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
172	
173	      # Extracts Jira issue keys (project key SFCC, per e2e/features/README.md's
174	      # @SFCC-NNN tag convention) referenced anywhere in the PR title, PR body,
175	      # or branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app uses to link a
176	      # PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own. Uses
177	      # `env:` rather than interpolating PR title/body directly into the run
178	      # script, since both are attacker-controllable text.
179	      # Consumed by e2e-browserstack: on a develop-targeted PR, BrowserStack
180	      # only runs when at least one key is found, scoped to that story's
181	      # Playwright tag(s). See testing.md > BrowserStack story scoping.
182	      - name: Detect Jira story keys
183	        id: jira
184	        env:
185	          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
186	          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
187	          BRANCH: ${{ github.head_ref }}
188	        run: |
189	          KEYS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$PR_TITLE" "$PR_BODY" "$BRANCH" \
190	            | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
191	          echo "keys=$KEYS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
192	
193	      # package.json/package-lock.json deliberately aren't in the e2e/vitest path
194	      # lists above: those two suites care about *runtime* behaviour, and most
195	      # lockfile churn (a devDependency bump, a transitive-dep resync) can't
196	      # affect what ships to the browser. Only a change to package.json's own
197	      # "dependencies" block (a real runtime dependency) should force them to
198	      # run. Storybook keeps the blanket file-level check above — it's cheap
199	      # enough that being conservative there doesn't matter.
200	      #
201	      # Diffs against the previous push (github.event.before, only present on
202	      # "synchronize"), not the base branch — same per-push reasoning as
203	      # since_last_remote_commit on "Get changed files" above. Without this,
204	      # a real dependency change on an earlier commit in the PR would leave
205	      # runtime_changed=true (and so e2e/vitest forced on) for every later
206	      # push, even a docs-only one, since it ORs into both outputs below.
207	      # Falls back to the base branch on "opened"/"reopened", where there's
208	      # no meaningful previous-push SHA yet.
209	      - name: Check whether runtime dependencies changed
210	        id: deps
211	        run: |
212	          if [[ "${{ github.event.action }}" == "synchronize" ]]; then
213	            BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.before }}"
214	            git fetch origin "$BASE_SHA" --depth=1
215	          else
216	            git fetch origin "${{ github.base_ref }}" --depth=1
217	            BASE_SHA="origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
218	          fi
219	          BASE_DEPS=$(git show "$BASE_SHA:package.json" | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(d).dependencies||{})))")
220	          HEAD_DEPS=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(require('./package.json').dependencies||{}))")
221	          if [ "$BASE_DEPS" != "$HEAD_DEPS" ]; then
222	            echo "runtime_changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
223	          else
224	            echo "runtime_changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
225	          fi

227	      - name: Persist e2e relevance for e2e-browserstack-preview.yml
228	        env:
229	          E2E_RELEVANT: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
230	        run: printf '{"e2e":"%s"}\n' "$E2E_RELEVANT" > "$E2E_RELEVANT_OUT"
231	
232	      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
233	        with:
234	          name: e2e-scope
235	          path: ${{ env.E2E_RELEVANT_OUT }}
236	          retention-days: 1

239	  # Unit tests — runs on every PR to develop and release/**
240	  # This project uses Vitest (see package.json "test": "vitest run").
241	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
242	  unit-tests:
243	    name: Unit tests (Vitest)
244	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
245	    needs: detect-changes
246	    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.vitest == 'true'
247	    permissions:
248	      contents: read
249	      pull-requests: write # to post/update the coverage summary comment below
250	    # No timeout-minutes previously meant this job defaulted to GitHub's
251	    # 360-minute ceiling — same unbounded-hang risk e2e-browserstack had
252	    # before a real run burned an hour on a stuck job (2026-08-25). Vitest
253	    # unit tests are fast and deterministic (the full suite runs in well
254	    # under a minute locally as of 2026-08-26), so 10 is generous headroom,
255	    # not a tight measured budget.
256	    timeout-minutes: 10
257	    steps:
258	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
259	
260	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
261	        with:
262	          node-version: '24'
263	
264	          cache: 'npm'
265	
266	      - name: Install dependencies
267	        run: npm install --include=dev
268	
269	      - name: Run Vitest unit tests with coverage
270	        run: npm run test:coverage
271	        env:
272	          CI: true
273	
274	      # Parses vitest's own JSON reporter output (test-results.json) and the
275	      # v8 coverage provider's json-summary (coverage/coverage-summary.json,
276	      # both produced by test:coverage's flags / vitest.config.ts's
277	      # coverage.reporter) into a single PR comment — pass/fail counts plus
278	      # a per-top-level-directory coverage breakdown. Upserts on an exact
279	      # HTML-comment marker so a redeploy updates the same comment instead
280	      # of spamming the thread, same pattern deploy-preview.yml's MRT
281	      # preview comment already uses. Runs even when the test step above
282	      # failed (always()) so a failing PR still gets the pass/fail count —
283	      # the coverage half of the comment degrades gracefully if the files
284	      # are missing (a hard crash before coverage was even written).
285	      - name: Post coverage/results summary to the PR
286	        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
287	        uses: actions/github-script@v7
288	        with:
289	          script: |
290	            const fs = require('fs')
291	
292	            const marker = '<!-- vitest-summary -->'
293	            let body = `${marker}\n## 🧪 Vitest Results\n\n`
294	
295	            let testResults = null
296	            try {
297	              testResults = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('test-results.json', 'utf8'))
298	            } catch (e) {
299	              body += `⚠️ Could not read test results (${e.message}) — the test run likely crashed before writing output.\n`
300	            }
301	
302	            if (testResults) {
303	              const { numTotalTests, numPassedTests, numFailedTests, numPendingTests, success } = testResults
304	              const icon = success ? '✅' : '❌'
305	              body += `${icon} **${numPassedTests}/${numTotalTests} passed**`
306	              if (numFailedTests) body += `, **${numFailedTests} failed**`
307	              if (numPendingTests) body += `, ${numPendingTests} skipped`
308	              body += '\n\n'
309	            }
310	
311	            let summary = null
312	            try {
313	              summary = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('coverage/coverage-summary.json', 'utf8'))
314	            } catch (e) {
315	              body += `_Coverage summary unavailable (${e.message})._\n`
316	            }
317	
318	            if (summary) {
319	              const total = summary.total
320	              body += `**Coverage — ${total.lines.pct}% lines** (${total.lines.covered}/${total.lines.total}), `
321	              body += `${total.branches.pct}% branches, ${total.functions.pct}% functions\n\n`
322	
323	              // Roll up per top-level directory under overrides/app/ — the
324	              // per-file table from the raw summary is too long to be a
325	              // useful PR comment; this is the same rollup grain the local
326	              // text reporter already prints.
327	              const dirs = {}
328	              for (const [filePath, data] of Object.entries(summary)) {
329	                if (filePath === 'total') continue
330	                const match = filePath.match(/overrides\/app\/([^/]+)\//)
331	                const dir = match ? match[1] : 'other'
332	                dirs[dir] ??= { total: 0, covered: 0 }
333	                dirs[dir].total += data.lines.total
334	                dirs[dir].covered += data.lines.covered
335	              }
336	
337	              body += '| Directory | Line coverage |\n|---|---|\n'
338	              for (const [dir, { total: t, covered: c }] of Object.entries(dirs).sort()) {
339	                const pct = t > 0 ? ((c / t) * 100).toFixed(1) : '100.0'
340	                body += `| \`app/${dir}\` | ${pct}% (${c}/${t}) |\n`
341	              }
342	              body += '\n<sub>Full HTML report: see the `vitest-coverage-report` artifact on this run.</sub>\n'
343	            }
344	
345	            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
346	              owner: context.repo.owner,
347	              repo: context.repo.repo,
348	              issue_number: context.issue.number,
349	              per_page: 100,
350	            })
351	            const existing = comments.find(
352	              (c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(marker) && c.user?.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
353	            )
354	            if (existing) {
355	              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
356	                owner: context.repo.owner,
357	                repo: context.repo.repo,
358	                comment_id: existing.id,
359	                body,
360	              })
361	            } else {
362	              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
363	                owner: context.repo.owner,
364	                repo: context.repo.repo,
365	                issue_number: context.issue.number,
366	                body,
367	              })
368	            }
369	
370	      - name: Upload coverage report
371	        if: always()
372	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
373	        with:
374	          name: vitest-coverage-report
375	          path: coverage/
376	          retention-days: 30

553	      - name: Upload dev server log
554	        if: always()
555	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
556	        with:
557	          name: dev-server-log
558	          path: dev-server.log
559	          retention-days: 30
560	
561	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
562	  # BrowserStack cross-browser regression — release/** only. Zephyr-linked,
563	  # cost-conscious. Complements the SIT gate (digital-sit.yml).
564	  #
565	  # Always the full e2e/tests/zimm suite, unscoped — a release aggregates
566	  # a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply. Zephyr
567	  # traceability still works in a full run since every test carries its
568	  # own @SFCC-NNN tag individually.
569	  #
570	  # The develop-PR, per-story path used to live here too, gated on a Jira
571	  # key and waiting (by polling) for this same commit's Deploy Preview run
572	  # so it could test the PR's own code instead of the static test tier.
573	  # That polling loop billed up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time
574	  # per push (2026-08-25, cost review) — moved to
575	  # e2e-browserstack-preview.yml instead, which is workflow_run-triggered
576	  # off Deploy Preview's completion and therefore never polls at all: it
577	  # doesn't start running (or billing) until the preview it needs already
578	  # exists. release/** PRs don't get a Deploy Preview run in the first
579	  # place (deploy-preview.yml excludes fix/release-* branches), so there's
580	  # nothing to wait for here — straight to the static test tier, always.
581	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
582	  e2e-browserstack:
583	    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
584	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
585	    needs: [unit-tests, detect-changes]
586	    # No timeout-minutes previously meant this job defaulted to GitHub's
587	    # 360-minute ceiling. A real run on PR #61 (2026-08-25) hung for over
588	    # an hour when BrowserStack requests were rejected (missing access-gate
589	    # header) instead of failing fast, and needed a manual force-cancel --
590	    # left alone it could have burned hours of billable minutes on a single
591	    # bad run. 30 covers install + the full unscoped suite with no waiting
592	    # on anything else.
593	    timeout-minutes: 30
594	    # RETAIL_APP_HOME lives as a Variable in the `test` GitHub Environment
595	    # (confirmed live via the Environments API, 2026-08-25) -- not a Secret,
596	    # and not under a `_SIT` suffix (there is no such secret anywhere in
597	    # this repo; `sit` the environment has no RETAIL_APP_HOME at all).
598	    # Without this binding the job can't see it, RETAIL_APP_HOME resolves
599	    # empty, and BasePage.goto() falls back to a hardcoded localhost URL
600	    # that BrowserStack's remote browsers can never reach anyway (real CI
601	    # failure on PR #61, 2026-08-25: every test failed page.goto with
602	    # net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED at http://localhost:3000/).
603	    environment: test
604	    # Same always()/skipped handling as e2e-localhost above.
605	    if: |
606	      always() &&
607	      needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
608	      (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped') &&
609	      contains(github.base_ref, 'release/')
610	
611	    steps:
612	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
613	
614	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
615	        with:
616	          node-version: '24'
617	
618	          cache: 'npm'
619	
620	      - name: Install dependencies
621	        run: npm install --include=dev
622	
623	      # release/** has no single primary story, so build-name always uses
624	      # the plain run-number naming (scripts/computeBuildName.mjs's
625	      # per-story Jira lookup is only meaningful on the develop-PR path,
626	      # which now lives in e2e-browserstack-preview.yml).
627	      - name: Compute build name
628	        id: build-name
629	        run: echo "name=${{ github.run_number }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
630	
631	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml downloads this rather than recomputing it
632	      # — see that workflow's own comment for why (spec-file-set drift
633	      # between what qa.yml saw and what the sync job's own checkout sees).
634	      - name: Persist build name for the Zephyr sync job
635	        env:
636	          BUILD_NAME: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
637	        run: printf '%s\n' "$BUILD_NAME" > browserstack-build-name.txt
638	
639	      - name: Upload build name artifact
640	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
641	        with:
642	          name: browserstack-build-name
643	          path: browserstack-build-name.txt
644	          retention-days: 7
645	
646	      - name: Run Zimmermann e2e on BrowserStack
647	        run: npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm
648	        env:
649	          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
650	          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
651	          SPRINT_NUMBER: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
652	          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}
653	          # The `test` tier is access-gated (confirmed with the developer,
654	          # 2026-08-25) -- without this header every request is rejected
655	          # before the page can load. See BasePage.js's applyExtraHeaders()
656	          # and testing.md > Access-gated preview URLs.
657	          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME }}
658	          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE }}
659	          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
660	          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
661	          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
662	          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
663	          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
664	          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
665	          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}
666	          SITE_ID: au  # Default — parameterise for multi-region runs
