file.content:
name: QA

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Detect which expensive suites are actually relevant to this diff.
  # Unit tests always run (cheap, and the fastest signal). Storybook and
  # E2E are skipped — not omitted from the trigger, actually run and
  # reported as "skipped" — when nothing under their relevant paths
  # changed, so a PR touching only e.g. .github/workflows/ or AGENTS.md
  # doesn't pay for a browser-driven Storybook build or a full Playwright
  # run against the dev org. A job-level `if:` is used deliberately
  # instead of an `on.pull_request.paths` filter: GitHub treats a skipped
  # required check as passing, but a workflow that never triggers at all
  # leaves a required check stuck "Expected" forever and blocks merging.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  detect-changes:
    name: Detect relevant changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      storybook: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.storybook_any_changed }}
      e2e: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
      vitest: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.vitest_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
      e2e_scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.e2e_scope }}
      jira_keys: ${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}
    env:
      # Written below and uploaded as an artifact so
      # e2e-browserstack-preview.yml (workflow_run off Deploy Preview,
      # develop-PR path) can pick up the same e2e-relevance gate this job
      # already computed, with a single non-looping API call — instead of
      # either re-running the whole tj-actions/changed-files matrix itself
      # or, worse, polling for it. See that workflow's own comment.
      E2E_RELEVANT_OUT: e2e-scope.json
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      # e2e_homepage below implements change-scoped E2E: on a develop-
      # targeted PR, e2e-localhost only runs the tests tagged for an area
      # (Playwright `{tag: '@<area>'}`, matching the Gherkin `@area` tag
      # documented in e2e/features/README.md) when EVERY changed path that
      # matters to E2E (the `e2e` group above) also falls inside that area's
      # own allow-list — see "Compute E2E scope" below for the subset check.
      # Anything outside every area's allow-list — a shared/global-impact
      # path (Global Shell, theme, hooks, config/, shared E2E infra — see
      # .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md and protectedFiles.md) or simply a path
      # no area has claimed yet — falls back to the full suite by
      # construction, deliberately, rather than needing its own deny-list to
      # maintain. Adding a new area: give it its own allow-list group here,
      # add the matching `@area` Playwright tag to its specs, and see
      # testing.md > Layer 3.
      - name: Get changed files
        id: changed
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          # Diff against the previous push on this PR branch, not the PR's
          # merge-base with develop/release. Without this, once ANY commit in
          # the PR's history touches a relevant path (e.g. config/**), every
          # later push re-triggers Storybook/E2E for the rest of the PR's
          # life — including a docs-only follow-up commit — because the
          # cumulative base...head diff still contains that earlier change.
          # Safe for required-status-check semantics: GitHub gates merge on
          # the latest SHA's checks, and a "skipped" job counts as passing
          # (see the always()/skipped handling on e2e-localhost below) — so
          # skipping here just means nothing e2e/storybook-relevant changed
          # since the last time those suites ran. Does not help across a
          # force-push/rebase (no well-defined "previous remote commit" in
          # that case) — not this project's normal workflow per AGENTS.md.
          since_last_remote_commit: true
          # Default separator is a space, which breaks the exact-line match
          # ("grep -qxF") "Compute E2E scope" does below against a multi-file
          # *_all_changed_files output — a space-joined string only matches
          # when there's exactly one file. Newline-joined lets grep -x match
          # each changed file independently regardless of how many there are.
          separator: "\n"
          files_yaml: |
            storybook:
              - 'overrides/app/components/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/**'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/**'
              - 'overrides/app/theme/**'
              - 'overrides/app/types/**'
              - '.storybook/**'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'package-lock.json'
            e2e:
              - 'overrides/**'
              - 'e2e/**'
              - 'config/**'
              - 'worker/**'
              - 'mobify.config.js'
              - 'playwright.config.*'
              - '.github/workflows/qa.yml'
              - '.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml'
              - 'browserstack.yml'
              - 'scripts/computeBuildName.mjs'
            e2e_homepage:
              - 'overrides/app/pages/home/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/header/**'
              - 'e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/**'
              - 'e2e/features/homepage/**'
              - 'e2e/support/pages/HomePage.js'
            vitest:
              - 'overrides/**'
              - 'vitest.config.*'
              - 'vitest.setup.ts'
              - 'tsconfig.json'
              - 'babel.config.js'

      # Resolve e2e_scope to "full", a single area name (e.g. "homepage")
      # consumed by e2e-localhost's --grep filter, or "skip". Defaults to
      # "full" on release/** (unchanged — a release PR aggregates a whole
      # sprint and gets the supervised, thorough pre-merge treatment per
      # releaseBranchesRules.md). On a develop-targeted PR, anything that
      # can't be narrowed to one area now resolves to "skip" instead of
      # "full" (changed 2026-08-25, at the developer's request) --
      # e2e-localhost no longer runs the entire suite on every PR whose
      # diff touches a shared/global path or an unclaimed area; that
      # broader regression coverage is deferred to the existing post-merge
      # P0 gates instead (deploy-test.yml's gate, digital-sit.yml's
      # playwright-p0 on release/**). Deliberate trade-off: a develop PR
      # that can't be scoped gets no PR-time E2E run at all now, only
      # unit tests / Storybook / BrowserStack (if a Jira key matches) —
      # full/non-P0 regressions on such a PR are caught later, at Test/SIT
      # deploy, not before merge. See testing.md > Change-scoped E2E.
      - name: Compute E2E scope
        id: scope
        # ALL/HOMEPAGE go through env: rather than being interpolated
        # directly into the script — a changed_files output is built from
        # real filenames in the diff, and interpolating one straight into
        # `run:` would let a filename containing quotes/shell syntax break
        # out of the assignment and execute on the runner (zizmor:
        # template-injection). Reading from env avoids that entirely.
        env:
          ALL: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_all_changed_files }}
          HOMEPAGE: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_homepage_all_changed_files }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.base_ref }}" == release/* ]]; then
            echo "e2e_scope=full" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          if [[ -z "$ALL" ]]; then
            echo "e2e_scope=skip" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Narrow to "homepage" only if every e2e-relevant changed file is
          # also in the homepage allow-list — a single file outside it (a
          # shared/global path, or one no area has claimed) skips the
          # PR-time run entirely, on purpose (see the step comment above).
          SCOPE="homepage"
          while IFS= read -r f; do
            [[ -z "$f" ]] && continue
            if ! grep -qxF "$f" <<< "$HOMEPAGE"; then
              SCOPE="skip"
              break
            fi
          done <<< "$ALL"
          echo "e2e_scope=$SCOPE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Extracts Jira issue keys (project key SFCC, per e2e/features/README.md's
      # @SFCC-NNN tag convention) referenced anywhere in the PR title, PR body,
      # or branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app uses to link a
      # PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own. Uses
      # `env:` rather than interpolating PR title/body directly into the run
      # script, since both are attacker-controllable text.
      # Consumed by e2e-browserstack: on a develop-targeted PR, BrowserStack
      # only runs when at least one key is found, scoped to that story's
      # Playwright tag(s). See testing.md > BrowserStack story scoping.
      - name: Detect Jira story keys
        id: jira
        env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
          BRANCH: ${{ github.head_ref }}
        run: |
          KEYS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$PR_TITLE" "$PR_BODY" "$BRANCH" \
            | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
          echo "keys=$KEYS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # package.json/package-lock.json deliberately aren't in the e2e/vitest path
      # lists above: those two suites care about *runtime* behaviour, and most
      # lockfile churn (a devDependency bump, a transitive-dep resync) can't
      # affect what ships to the browser. Only a change to package.json's own
      # "dependencies" block (a real runtime dependency) should force them to
      # run. Storybook keeps the blanket file-level check above — it's cheap
      # enough that being conservative there doesn't matter.
      #
      # Diffs against the previous push (github.event.before, only present on
      # "synchronize"), not the base branch — same per-push reasoning as
      # since_last_remote_commit on "Get changed files" above. Without this,
      # a real dependency change on an earlier commit in the PR would leave
      # runtime_changed=true (and so e2e/vitest forced on) for every later
      # push, even a docs-only one, since it ORs into both outputs below.
      # Falls back to the base branch on "opened"/"reopened", where there's
      # no meaningful previous-push SHA yet.
      - name: Check whether runtime dependencies changed
        id: deps
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ github.event.action }}" == "synchronize" ]]; then
            BASE_SHA="${{ github.event.before }}"
            git fetch origin "$BASE_SHA" --depth=1
          else
            git fetch origin "${{ github.base_ref }}" --depth=1
            BASE_SHA="origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
          fi
          BASE_DEPS=$(git show "$BASE_SHA:package.json" | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>console.log(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(d).dependencies||{})))")
          HEAD_DEPS=$(node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(require('./package.json').dependencies||{}))")
          if [ "$BASE_DEPS" != "$HEAD_DEPS" ]; then
            echo "runtime_changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "runtime_changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Persist e2e relevance for e2e-browserstack-preview.yml
        env:
          E2E_RELEVANT: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.e2e_any_changed == 'true' || steps.deps.outputs.runtime_changed == 'true' }}
        run: printf '{"e2e":"%s"}\n' "$E2E_RELEVANT" > "$E2E_RELEVANT_OUT"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: e2e-scope
          path: ${{ env.E2E_RELEVANT_OUT }}
          retention-days: 1

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Unit tests — runs on every PR to develop and release/**
  # This project uses Vitest (see package.json "test": "vitest run").
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit tests (Vitest)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.vitest == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write # to post/update the coverage summary comment below
    # No timeout-minutes previously meant this job defaulted to GitHub's
    # 360-minute ceiling — same unbounded-hang risk e2e-browserstack had
    # before a real run burned an hour on a stuck job (2026-08-25). Vitest
    # unit tests are fast and deterministic (the full suite runs in well
    # under a minute locally as of 2026-08-26), so 10 is generous headroom,
    # not a tight measured budget.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Run Vitest unit tests with coverage
        run: npm run test:coverage
        env:
          CI: true

      # Parses vitest's own JSON reporter output (test-results.json) and the
      # v8 coverage provider's json-summary (coverage/coverage-summary.json,
      # both produced by test:coverage's flags / vitest.config.ts's
      # coverage.reporter) into a single PR comment — pass/fail counts plus
      # a per-top-level-directory coverage breakdown. Upserts on an exact
      # HTML-comment marker so a redeploy updates the same comment instead
      # of spamming the thread, same pattern deploy-preview.yml's MRT
      # preview comment already uses. Runs even when the test step above
      # failed (always()) so a failing PR still gets the pass/fail count —
      # the coverage half of the comment degrades gracefully if the files
      # are missing (a hard crash before coverage was even written).
      - name: Post coverage/results summary to the PR
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require('fs')

            const marker = '<!-- vitest-summary -->'
            let body = `${marker}\n## 🧪 Vitest Results\n\n`

            let testResults = null
            try {
              testResults = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('test-results.json', 'utf8'))
            } catch (e) {
              body += `⚠️ Could not read test results (${e.message}) — the test run likely crashed before writing output.\n`
            }

            if (testResults) {
              const { numTotalTests, numPassedTests, numFailedTests, numPendingTests, success } = testResults
              const icon = success ? '✅' : '❌'
              body += `${icon} **${numPassedTests}/${numTotalTests} passed**`
              if (numFailedTests) body += `, **${numFailedTests} failed**`
              if (numPendingTests) body += `, ${numPendingTests} skipped`
              body += '\n\n'
            }

            let summary = null
            try {
              summary = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('coverage/coverage-summary.json', 'utf8'))
            } catch (e) {
              body += `_Coverage summary unavailable (${e.message})._\n`
            }

            if (summary) {
              const total = summary.total
              body += `**Coverage — ${total.lines.pct}% lines** (${total.lines.covered}/${total.lines.total}), `
              body += `${total.branches.pct}% branches, ${total.functions.pct}% functions\n\n`

              // Roll up per top-level directory under overrides/app/ — the
              // per-file table from the raw summary is too long to be a
              // useful PR comment; this is the same rollup grain the local
              // text reporter already prints.
              const dirs = {}
              for (const [filePath, data] of Object.entries(summary)) {
                if (filePath === 'total') continue
                const match = filePath.match(/overrides\/app\/([^/]+)\//)
                const dir = match ? match[1] : 'other'
                dirs[dir] ??= { total: 0, covered: 0 }
                dirs[dir].total += data.lines.total
                dirs[dir].covered += data.lines.covered
              }

              body += '| Directory | Line coverage |\n|---|---|\n'
              for (const [dir, { total: t, covered: c }] of Object.entries(dirs).sort()) {
                const pct = t > 0 ? ((c / t) * 100).toFixed(1) : '100.0'
                body += `| \`app/${dir}\` | ${pct}% (${c}/${t}) |\n`
              }
              body += '\n<sub>Full HTML report: see the `vitest-coverage-report` artifact on this run.</sub>\n'
            }

            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              per_page: 100,
            })
            const existing = comments.find(
              (c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(marker) && c.user?.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
            )
            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              })
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              })
            }

      - name: Upload coverage report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: vitest-coverage-report
          path: coverage/
          retention-days: 30

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Storybook interaction + a11y tests — runs on every PR to develop
  # and release/**. Exercises play() functions and @storybook/addon-a11y
  # component-level checks headless. Runs in parallel with unit-tests.
  # Runner: @storybook/test-runner (Playwright-based). Storybook is built
  # to storybook-static/, served by http-server, tested by test-storybook.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  storybook-test:
    name: Storybook interaction & a11y tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: detect-changes
    if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Build Storybook
        run: npm run build-storybook

      - name: Run Storybook interaction and a11y tests
        run: |
          npx http-server storybook-static --port 6006 --silent &
          npx wait-on http://127.0.0.1:6006 --timeout 60000
          node_modules/.bin/test-storybook --ci --url http://127.0.0.1:6006
        env:
          CI: true

      - name: Upload Storybook test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: storybook-test-results
          path: storybook-test-results/
          retention-days: 30

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Playwright E2E — every PR to develop and release/**.
  # Boots the PWA Kit dev server on localhost:3000 against the SFCC dev
  # org (real API, no mocks). Runs desktop Chromium + mobile Chrome.
  # BrowserStack cross-browser coverage is a separate job (release only).
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  e2e-localhost:
    name: Playwright E2E (localhost)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Binds this job to the "dev" GitHub Environment so vars.* below resolves
    # against it. Since scripts/switchEnv.mjs's `push <tier>` now pushes a
    # shared+tier merge (see that script's buildPushEntries), "dev" alone is
    # self-sufficient — no second environment binding needed for shared-scope
    # values like the Commerce API short code / site id. No protection rules
    # are configured on "dev" (confirmed via `gh api repos/.../environments/dev`),
    # so this doesn't add an approval gate or branch restriction to PR runs.
    environment: dev
    # Without this, a genuinely unreachable SFCC dev org (or any other
    # unbounded hang outside Playwright's own per-test timeout/retry
    # budget) rides GitHub's default 6-hour job ceiling instead of failing
    # fast with a clear signal. 15 is measured, not padded: setup (checkout
    # -> deps -> browsers -> dev server) took ~1m30s and a real full-retry
    # SFCC-dev-org-down failure took 12m13s on the Playwright step alone
    # (run 29178792019, job 86612779025, 2026-07-12) — 15 gives that ~1.5min
    # of margin for normal CI variance without hiding a dead job for long.
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: [unit-tests, detect-changes]
    # Re-enabled 2026-07-16 on bugfix/ci-e2e-test to actively debug the
    # homepage smoke test failure — now confirmed fixed (see
    # .docs/memory/projectState.md) with better diagnostics: an HTML report
    # now gets generated (playwright.config.js), while Playwright retains
    # its default two retries for each CI iteration.
    # unit-tests may now report "skipped" rather than "success" (see
    # detect-changes above) — GitHub's implicit success() over all `needs`
    # would otherwise treat a skipped unit-tests as blocking this job too.
    # !cancelled() bypasses that default so we can explicitly allow skipped
    # — unlike always(), it still stops this job from continuing on a
    # cancelled workflow run (e.g. superseded by a newer push), instead of
    # burning a 15-minute runner slot on a run nobody's waiting on.
    if: |
      !cancelled() &&
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e_scope != 'skip' &&
      (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped')
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Start dev server
        # Output wasn't captured anywhere before — a backgrounded process's
        # stdout/stderr doesn't show up in the step's own log. Redirecting to
        # a file (uploaded below, always) is the only way to see an SSR
        # crash/error server-side instead of just the client-visible symptom
        # (a non-200 response, or a page that never finishes rendering).
        run: npm start > dev-server.log 2>&1 &
        env:
          # DEPLOY_TARGET (not ENVIRONMENT_NAME) is what
          # @salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime's getConfig() reads to pick
          # config/<target>.js — must be a real process env var before
          # `pwa-kit-dev start` launches, since getConfig() resolves it
          # before config/default.js's own .env-loading code ever runs.
          DEPLOY_TARGET: dev
          ENVIRONMENT_NAME: dev
          # PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET stays on the repo Secret (encrypted)
          # rather than the "dev" Environment's plaintext Variable copy of
          # the same key — no reason to downgrade now that environment: dev
          # also exposes it via vars.*.
          PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET }}
          COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID }}
          COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID }}
          COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE }}
          COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID: ${{ vars.COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID }}

      - name: Wait for dev server
        run: npx wait-on http://localhost:3000 --timeout 120000

      - name: Wait for webpack build to finish
        # wait-on above only confirms the port is accepting connections —
        # pwa-kit-dev answers requests (redirects, in practice) before the
        # client bundle has actually finished compiling, so Playwright could
        # start racing a still-building app and fail on missing elements
        # with no clear signal why. "webpack built client" in dev-server.log
        # is the real readiness marker; polling for it adapts to actual
        # build time instead of guessing a fixed delay.
        run: |
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
            grep -q "webpack built client" dev-server.log && exit 0
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "Timed out waiting for webpack build to finish after 120s" >&2
          exit 1

      - name: Run Playwright (desktop + mobile)
        # e2e_scope is "full" or an area name (e.g. "homepage") computed by
        # detect-changes — see the comments on that job's "Get changed
        # files" / "Compute E2E scope" steps and testing.md > Layer 3.
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e_scope }}" == "full" ]]; then
            npx playwright test --project=chromium --project=mobile-chrome
          else
            npx playwright test --project=chromium --project=mobile-chrome --grep "@${{ needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e_scope }}"
          fi
        env:
          SITE_ID: au
          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report-localhost
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload dev server log
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dev-server-log
          path: dev-server.log
          retention-days: 30

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # BrowserStack cross-browser regression — release/** only. Zephyr-linked,
  # cost-conscious. Complements the SIT gate (digital-sit.yml).
  #
  # Always the full e2e/tests/zimm suite, unscoped — a release aggregates
  # a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply. Zephyr
  # traceability still works in a full run since every test carries its
  # own @SFCC-NNN tag individually.
  #
  # The develop-PR, per-story path used to live here too, gated on a Jira
  # key and waiting (by polling) for this same commit's Deploy Preview run
  # so it could test the PR's own code instead of the static test tier.
  # That polling loop billed up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time
  # per push (2026-08-25, cost review) — moved to
  # e2e-browserstack-preview.yml instead, which is workflow_run-triggered
  # off Deploy Preview's completion and therefore never polls at all: it
  # doesn't start running (or billing) until the preview it needs already
  # exists. release/** PRs don't get a Deploy Preview run in the first
  # place (deploy-preview.yml excludes fix/release-* branches), so there's
  # nothing to wait for here — straight to the static test tier, always.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  e2e-browserstack:
    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [unit-tests, detect-changes]
    # No timeout-minutes previously meant this job defaulted to GitHub's
    # 360-minute ceiling. A real run on PR #61 (2026-08-25) hung for over
    # an hour when BrowserStack requests were rejected (missing access-gate
    # header) instead of failing fast, and needed a manual force-cancel --
    # left alone it could have burned hours of billable minutes on a single
    # bad run. 30 covers install + the full unscoped suite with no waiting
    # on anything else.
    timeout-minutes: 30
    # RETAIL_APP_HOME lives as a Variable in the `test` GitHub Environment
    # (confirmed live via the Environments API, 2026-08-25) -- not a Secret,
    # and not under a `_SIT` suffix (there is no such secret anywhere in
    # this repo; `sit` the environment has no RETAIL_APP_HOME at all).
    # Without this binding the job can't see it, RETAIL_APP_HOME resolves
    # empty, and BasePage.goto() falls back to a hardcoded localhost URL
    # that BrowserStack's remote browsers can never reach anyway (real CI
    # failure on PR #61, 2026-08-25: every test failed page.goto with
    # net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED at http://localhost:3000/).
    environment: test
    # Same always()/skipped handling as e2e-localhost above.
    if: |
      always() &&
      needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
      (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped') &&
      contains(github.base_ref, 'release/')

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # release/** has no single primary story, so build-name always uses
      # the plain run-number naming (scripts/computeBuildName.mjs's
      # per-story Jira lookup is only meaningful on the develop-PR path,
      # which now lives in e2e-browserstack-preview.yml).
      - name: Compute build name
        id: build-name
        run: echo "name=${{ github.run_number }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # zephyr-results-sync.yml downloads this rather than recomputing it
      # — see that workflow's own comment for why (spec-file-set drift
      # between what qa.yml saw and what the sync job's own checkout sees).
      - name: Persist build name for the Zephyr sync job
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
        run: printf '%s\n' "$BUILD_NAME" > browserstack-build-name.txt

      - name: Upload build name artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: browserstack-build-name
          path: browserstack-build-name.txt
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Run Zimmermann e2e on BrowserStack
        run: npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm
        env:
          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
          SPRINT_NUMBER: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}
          # The `test` tier is access-gated (confirmed with the developer,
          # 2026-08-25) -- without this header every request is rejected
          # before the page can load. See BasePage.js's applyExtraHeaders()
          # and testing.md > Access-gated preview URLs.
          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME }}
          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE }}
          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}
          SITE_ID: au  # Default — parameterise for multi-region runs

file.content:
name: Protected File Guard

# Server-side enforcement of the tier/squad model. The client-side
# .claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh is non-blocking — this workflow is the
# authoritative gate at PR time.

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - main
      - 'release/**'
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

jobs:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 1 — Hard block: PR targeting wrong branch.
  # Kept as its OWN job, unmerged with the informational checks below —
  # "🔴 Branch Target Check" is a REQUIRED status check on develop, main,
  # and release/** branch protection (confirmed live via the Branch
  # Protection API, 2026-08-25). Folding it into a combined job would
  # rename what GitHub sees as reporting that check, silently breaking
  # required-status-check enforcement (merges would block forever until
  # someone updated the branch protection settings to the new name) —
  # not worth the minutes saving. The other three checks below are not
  # required by any branch protection rule (confirmed the same way),
  # so those are safe to combine into one job.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  branch-target-guard:
    name: '🔴 Branch Target Check'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Block direct PRs to main from feature branches
        # github.base_ref/head_ref are attacker-controllable (a branch name
        # can contain shell metacharacters, e.g. $(...) command substitution)
        # and actionlint flags direct interpolation into an inline script as
        # a script-injection vector -- delivered via env: instead, same
        # pattern already used throughout qa.yml/deploy-preview.yml
        # (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-26).
        env:
          BASE: ${{ github.base_ref }}
          HEAD: ${{ github.head_ref }}
        run: |
          echo "Base branch: $BASE"
          echo "Head branch: $HEAD"

          # Feature branches must not go directly to main
          if [[ "$BASE" == "main" && "$HEAD" == feature/* ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            echo "🔴 INVALID BRANCH TARGET"
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            echo ""
            echo "Feature branches must target 'develop', not 'main'."
            echo ""
            echo "Correct flow: feature/* → develop → (release/*) → main"
            echo ""
            echo "Please update the base branch of this PR to 'develop'."
            echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "✅ Branch target is valid."

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # JOB 2 — Informational checks, combined (2026-08-25): Tier 1 warning,
  # Tier 2 warning, and cross-squad boundary detection used to be three
  # separate jobs, each paying GitHub Actions' 1-minute-per-job billing
  # floor even though each did only a few seconds of real work — roughly
  # 700 minutes/month of pure rounding overhead across this repo's PR
  # volume (see the 2026-08-25 Actions-minutes analysis). None of the
  # three is a required status check (confirmed live via the Branch
  # Protection API), so merging them changes nothing GitHub enforces —
  # only "🔴 Branch Target Check" above had to stay separate. Order
  # matters here: each check still runs and reports (posts its own
  # comment / log warning) regardless of whether an earlier one found
  # something, matching the old all-jobs-run-independently behavior —
  # nothing here calls exit 1, so a finding in one check never skips
  # the next.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  file-tier-checks:
    name: '🟡 File Tier & Squad Boundary Checks'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

      - name: Get changed Tier 1 files
        id: tier1
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          base_sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          files_yaml: |
            tier1:
              # Design tokens — owner: UI Designer
              - 'overrides/app/theme/foundation/**'
              - 'overrides/app/theme/index.ts'
              # Commerce SDK hooks (overrides surface) — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.*'
              # Runtime & integration config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'config/**'
              - 'overrides/app/ssr.*'
              - 'worker/main.*'
              - 'mobify.config.js'
              - 'package.json'
              - 'package-lock.json'
              # Test & tooling config — owner: Integration Lead
              - 'vitest.config.*'
              - 'playwright.config.*'
              - '.storybook/**'
              - 'tests/lighthouserc.*'
              - 'lighthouserc.*'
              # CI/CD — owner: Integration Lead
              - '.github/workflows/**'
              # Governance — owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead
              - 'AGENTS.md'
              - 'CLAUDE.md'
              - 'CODEOWNERS'
              - '.claude/rules/**'
              - '.claude/settings.json'
              - 'coderabbit.yaml'
              - '.coderabbit/**'
              - 'semgrep.yml'
              - 'scripts/hooks/**'

      - name: Warn if Tier 1 files changed (informational — not a merge block)
        if: steps.tier1.outputs.tier1_any_changed == 'true'
        run: |
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo "🔴 TIER 1 PROTECTED FILES DETECTED IN THIS PR"
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
          echo ""
          echo "The following frozen files have been modified:"
          echo ""
          echo "${{ steps.tier1.outputs.tier1_all_changed_files }}" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/  ❌ /'
          echo ""
          echo "These files require an approving code-owner review before merge."
          echo "This check is informational — the actual merge block is CODEOWNERS +"
          echo "the required code-owner review, enforced by GitHub natively."
          echo ""
          echo "REQUIRED ACTIONS before this PR can be merged:"
          echo "  1. Get an approving review (not just a comment) from a member of"
          echo "     @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers — CODEOWNERS auto-requests this."
          echo "  2. Contact the correct owner using the table below"
          echo ""
          echo "OWNER CONTACT MAP:"
          echo "  overrides/app/theme/foundation/      → UI Designer      (#design-system)"
          echo "  overrides/app/theme/index.ts         → UI Designer      (#design-system)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-current-*   → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein    → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud   → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-tok → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  config/                             → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  overrides/app/ssr.*                 → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  worker/main.*                       → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  mobify.config.js                    → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  package.json (root)                 → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  vitest/playwright/.storybook config → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  .github/workflows/                  → Integration Lead (#integration)"
          echo "  AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / CODEOWNERS  → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  .claude/rules/ / .claude/settings   → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  coderabbit.yaml / .coderabbit/      → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo "  semgrep.yml / scripts/hooks/        → Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead (#dev-team)"
          echo ""
          echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"

      - name: Pass — no Tier 1 files changed
        if: steps.tier1.outputs.tier1_any_changed == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "✅ No Tier 1 protected files detected in this PR."

      - name: Get changed Tier 2 files
        id: tier2
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          base_sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          files_yaml: |
            tier2:
              # Global shell — both squads
              - 'overrides/app/components/header/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/footer/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/list-menu/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/seo/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/_app/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/_app-config/**'
              - 'overrides/app/routes.*'
              # Shared product components — Squad B primary, Squad A notified
              - 'overrides/app/components/product-tile/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/product-item/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/display-price/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/image-gallery/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/swatch-group/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/recommended-products/**'
              # Shared commerce components — Squad A primary, Squad B notified
              - 'overrides/app/components/order-summary/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/promo-code/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/**'
              # Theme component styles — UI Designer
              - 'overrides/app/theme/components/**'
              # Translations — Integration / SI Partner
              - 'translations/**'
              - 'overrides/app/static/translations/**'
              # Shared hooks — both squads
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-currency.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-dnt-notification.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-app-origin.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-selected-store.*'

      - name: Post Tier 2 warning comment on PR
        if: steps.tier2.outputs.tier2_any_changed == 'true'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const files = `${{ steps.tier2.outputs.tier2_all_changed_files }}`
              .split(' ')
              .filter(Boolean)
              .map(f => `- \`${f}\``)
              .join('\n');

            const body = `## 🟡 Tier 2 Protected Files Detected

            This PR modifies shared components or hooks that are used across multiple features or squads.
            This is **not a merge block** — but it requires a second-developer review before merging.

            **Files affected:**
            ${files}

            **Required before merge:**
            - [ ] A developer from the **other squad** (not the PR author's squad) has reviewed and approved
            - [ ] The UI Designer has been notified if \`overrides/app/theme/components/\` is included
            - [ ] The Integration / SI Partner has been notified if \`translations/\` is included
            - [ ] No prop signature or export changes have been made without updating all consumers

            **Why this matters:** These files are imported by components in both Squad A and Squad B.
            A breaking change here — even a small one — will affect both squads simultaneously.

            _This comment is auto-generated by the Protected File Guard workflow._`;

            // Check if we already posted this comment to avoid duplicates
            const comments = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
            });

            const existing = comments.data.find(c =>
              c.body.includes('Tier 2 Protected Files Detected') &&
              c.user.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
            );

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

      - name: Pass — no Tier 2 files changed
        if: steps.tier2.outputs.tier2_any_changed == 'false'
        run: |
          echo "✅ No Tier 2 protected files detected in this PR."

      - name: Detect Squad A files changed
        id: squad-a
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          base_sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          files_yaml: |
            squad_a:
              - 'overrides/app/pages/cart/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/checkout/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/checkout-one-click/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/confirmation/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/sf-payments-express/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/sf-payments-express-buttons/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/multiship/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/bonus-product-view-modal/**'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-checkout-auto-select.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-multiship.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-pickup-shipment.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-sf-payments.*'

      - name: Detect Squad B files changed
        id: squad-b
        uses: tj-actions/changed-files@2d756ea4c53f7f6b397767d8723b3a10a9f35bf2 # v44
        with:
          base_sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          files_yaml: |
            squad_b:
              - 'overrides/app/pages/home/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/product-list/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/search/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/account/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/wishlist/**'
              - 'overrides/app/pages/store-locator/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/search/**'
              - 'overrides/app/components/store-locator/**'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-product-view-modal.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-derived-product.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-variant.*'
              - 'overrides/app/hooks/use-wish-list.*'

      - name: Warn on cross-squad PR
        if: |
          steps.squad-a.outputs.squad_a_any_changed == 'true' &&
          steps.squad-b.outputs.squad_b_any_changed == 'true'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const squadAFiles = `${{ steps.squad-a.outputs.squad_a_all_changed_files }}`
              .split(' ').filter(Boolean).map(f => `- \`${f}\``).join('\n');
            const squadBFiles = `${{ steps.squad-b.outputs.squad_b_all_changed_files }}`
              .split(' ').filter(Boolean).map(f => `- \`${f}\``).join('\n');

            const body = `## ⚠️ Cross-Squad Boundary Detected

1	# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)
2	
3	> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**
4	> Every file created or modified under `overrides/` **must** use `.ts` or `.tsx`.
5	> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
6	> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.
7	
8	Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.
9	
10	Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).
11	
12	## Branch Rules
13	
14	**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.
15	
16	| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       | Allowed?      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
17	| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
18	| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Primary working context for new work                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
19	| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene                                                                                                                                                                                |
20	| `release/*`               | `develop`              | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch                                                                                                                                                                          |
21	| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes        | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
22	| `hotfix/*`                | `main`                 | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ✅ Yes        | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift                                                                                                                                                                 |
23	| `develop`                 | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
24	| `main`                    | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
25	
26	> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.
27	
28	## Hard Rules
29	
30	1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.
31	2. **Never modify a Tier 1 file** without the developer explicitly naming it in the prompt and confirming owner approval — unless the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) applies. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md).
32	3. **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — all design token changes go through the UI designer.
33	4. **Never modify `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, or `worker/main.js`.** These are absolute — the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) does not apply to them, regardless of approver status. `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 CI/CD config and instead follows the standard Hard Rule #2 process (verified-session exception applies).
34	5. **Never refactor upward.** Fixing a bug in a component does not mean touching the hook or utility it calls.
35	6. **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
36	7. **Never add or remove packages** from `package.json` without integration team approval. When approved, always use `npm install` rather than editing `package.json` directly.
37	8. **Never modify test configuration files** (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `tests/lighthouserc.js`).
38	9. **Never delete files** without being explicitly asked in the current prompt. You may propose deletion and let a human confirm.
39	10. **Never touch more than one protection tier** in a single change without stopping to confirm scope with the developer.
40	11. **Never assume a hook is safe to modify** because it has a simple name — check the frozenFiles list first.
41	12. **When requirements are unclear, ask one clarifying question at a time.** Do not proceed with assumptions and do not batch questions. Wait for the answer before asking the next question or writing any code.
42	13. **Never use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`** on `release/**`, `main`, or `develop`. This flag bypasses all edit confirmations and is only permitted in CI automation contexts, never in interactive developer sessions on shared or protected branches.
43	14. **Never reference code from a later sprint.** Check [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) before scoping any new work. If a task depends on a component, hook, or integration that belongs to a later sprint, stop and ask whether to build a placeholder or whether that sprint is already complete.
44	15. **Never create a git commit, push to remote, or open/close a PR** without the developer explicitly requesting it in the current prompt. Resuming from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit — wait for an explicit ask.
45	
46	## Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced
47	
48	Claude Code's confirmation prompt before touching a Tier 1 file (Hard Rule #2) is a workflow
49	safeguard, not the security boundary — it can't be, since it only governs what Claude itself
50	does, not what any other tool or a direct `git push` can do. The real enforcement is server-side:
51	
52	- [CODEOWNERS](../CODEOWNERS) routes every Tier 1 path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, a
53	  real GitHub org team.
54	- Branch protection on `develop`/`main`/`release/**` requires an approving code-owner review
55	  before merge — this is the actual gate, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
56	  involvement, so it can't be affected by a broken or delayed CI run.
57	- `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`'s `tier1-guard` job posts a loud warning and an
58	  owner-contact-map on any PR touching a Tier 1 path. It is **not** a required status check —
59	  GitHub locked down cross-run check-run updates in Feb 2025, which made a "hard-fail until
60	  approved, then flip to pass on review" required check impossible to implement reliably (a
61	  fresh commit is needed to re-evaluate it, since a later review can't flip an earlier run's
62	  result). The CODEOWNERS-based review requirement above is the real, working block.
63	
64	Because the actual gate lives in GitHub, not in Claude's judgement, this file does not encode
65	personal names or email addresses as a bypass condition — a string in a shared, version-controlled
66	file is not an identity check; anyone (or any other Claude session) could satisfy it by typing it.
67	Instead, Claude may verify the real, authenticated identity behind the current session:
68	
69	- Before pausing to ask for Tier 1 confirmation, run `gh api user --jq .login`, then check
70	  `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login'` (or check for `admin`
71	  via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/collaborators/<login>/permission`). If that GitHub
72	  login is a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or holds repo admin, Claude may proceed
73	  with the edit after stating which Tier 1 file is being touched and why — no separate
74	  confirmation message is required, since GitHub already recognises that account as an approver.
75	- If the authenticated login is **not** a member/admin, Claude must still stop per Hard Rule #2:
76	  name the file, and require the developer to secure an approving review from
77	  `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` before the PR can merge. CODEOWNERS auto-requests that review
78	  and branch protection blocks the merge without it, regardless of what `tier1-guard` reports.
79	- This check only ever reduces _how many times Claude pauses to ask_. It changes nothing about
80	  what GitHub will actually allow to merge — that's deliberate, so a compromised or careless
81	  Claude session can't grant itself write access to a frozen file.
82	
83	## Coding Task Workflow
84	
85	Every coding task follows these four steps in order. Do not skip ahead — pause at the marked points and wait for the user.
86	
87	1. **Clarify requirements.** Identify every gap, ambiguity, or contradiction in the request and the relevant `.docs/`. Confirm each one with the user before moving on — no assumptions. See Hard Rule #12: ask one question at a time.
88	2. **Plan.** State the files you intend to touch, _why_ each one is being touched, and any base template files that will need to be copied to `overrides/`. Then **pause** and wait for the user to confirm the plan. See the **Minimal changes** rule below.
89	3. **Copy first (if any).** For every base template file identified in step 2, follow the **Copy-first rule** in the Rules section. Then **pause** and let the user test and stage the override files before any functional changes.
90	4. **Implement.** Make the planned modifications. Remove the `console.log` markers from step 3 once the user confirms the overrides are rendering. Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review: confirm the CLI is installed and authenticated (`coderabbit auth status`; if not authenticated, `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` — see `.env.sample`), then `cr review --light --base develop` (use `main` instead on a `release/**`/`hotfix/**` branch). **The CLI is required, not optional** — if it isn't installed or authenticated, stop and have the developer install it (https://www.coderabbit.ai/cli) and run `npm run env -- init` to pull the shared key, rather than committing without a local review. The review itself is still advisory relative to the actual merge gate (the GitHub PR review remains the real gate) — use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth fixing before the commit vs. leaving it for the PR review to catch, but the review must actually run.
91	
92	**Responding to a CodeRabbit PR review.** Once CodeRabbit finishes reviewing an open PR, always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every finding, whether it's fixed or not — CodeRabbit's learning feature picks up patterns from PR conversation, so silence teaches it nothing and an explanation teaches it to stop flagging the same non-issue. A fix commit alone, with no reply posted on the thread, doesn't count. For a finding that gets fixed, a short in-thread reply confirming the fix (referencing the commit is fine) is enough. For a finding that is *not* being fixed because it conflicts with this repo's own rules/docs/architecture (e.g. a Tier 1 exception that was actually followed correctly, an intentional design tradeoff already recorded in `.docs/`) — reply in-thread explaining the specific rule or doc that justifies not changing it, so CodeRabbit's learning has the context to recognise the same pattern next time instead of re-flagging it. Never silently dismiss a finding without a reply.
93	
94	## When to Stop and Ask a Human
95	
96	| Trigger                                                                      | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
97	| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
98	| Task requires a Tier 1 file                                                  | Check the authenticated `gh` identity against `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`/admin (see [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced)). If verified, name the file and proceed. Otherwise stop and require named owner approval. |
99	| A shared hook needs its function signature changed                           | Stop. Requires a team RFC.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
100	| A new package dependency is needed                                           | Stop. Integration team must approve.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
101	| Current branch is `develop` or `main`                                        | Stop immediately. No changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
102	| Change affects more than one regional site config                            | Stop. Integration team sign-off required.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
103	| Change spans multiple protection tiers                                       | Stop. Confirm scope with the developer before continuing.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
104	| Requirement is missing, ambiguous, contradictory, or unconfirmed in `.docs/` | Stop. Flag, propose, wait for approval (see Requirements section).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
105	
106	## Multi-site & Routing
107	
108	The SFCC sites are hard routing and config boundaries — **never bleed config across sites.** Never assume a storefront's routing, URL prefix, checkout ownership, or consent defaults without checking [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md).
109	
110	## Commands
111	
112	- `npm start` — local dev at http://localhost:3000. **Do not run!** Ask the user to restart if needed.
113	- `npm run build`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run push` (Managed Runtime deploy)
114	
115	## Accessibility
116	
117	Target WCAG 2.2 AA. Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible — document why.
118	
119	## Rules
120	
121	*Day-to-day code-writing conventions live in `.claude/rules/` and load automatically:
122	[conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) (cross-cutting: naming, imports, DRY, security),
123	[typescript.md](.claude/rules/typescript.md) (TS idioms), [css.md](.claude/rules/css.md)
124	(Chakra tokens, `.scss`), and [components.md](.claude/rules/components.md)
125	(component/hook/utility structure, Storybook categorisation, composition). The rules below
126	are project-specific behaviours and security guardrails that don't fit there.*
127	
128	- **No mocking:** All data must come from the live Commerce Cloud API via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks. No MSW or hardcoded fixtures in production paths.
129	- **Environment variables:** Never hardcode secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials anywhere in the codebase. Non-personal shared/tier values may additionally be centrally published via `npm run env -- push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only) to this repo's GitHub Environments — genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal`, e.g. your own Atlassian or Contentful CMA token) must never be pushed.
130	- **Comments:** Do not remove existing commented-out code or comments (except when removing the corresponding code) — leave for the user to delete manually. (For _new_ comments introduced in a PR, see conventions.md.)
131	- **Icons:** Use `overrides/app/components/icons` — this is the single source of truth for all icons (Zimmermann custom and base PWA). Do not import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly. If a required icon is missing from the overrides set, ask the user — do not substitute a visually different one.
132	- **Styling:** Chakra UI component props first; use a `.scss` file alongside the component only when Chakra props are insufficient. The `overrides/app/theme/` folder is the source of truth — brand tokens in `foundation/` (Tier 1), one file per component override in `components/` (Tier 2), composed in `index.ts`. Register a new component override in `theme/components/index.ts`.
133	- **Minimal changes:** Make the smallest change that fully achieves the task. Do not remove or replace existing base template functionality unless explicitly instructed. When a larger change (e.g., a refactor for cleanliness) seems beneficial, propose it and wait for user confirmation — never do it silently.
134	- **Copy-first rule:** For any task that requires overriding base template files that do not yet exist in `overrides/`, the very first step is to prepare all of them at once: (1) copy each file from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`, (2) convert each to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`) and update relevant imports, (3) run `npx tsc --noEmit`, (4) add a temporary `console.log` to each copied file identifying it (e.g. `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')`) so the user can verify the override is rendering instead of the base component, then **stop and present the converted files to the user to test**. 136	## Consent & Marketing
137	
138	- **Didomi:** Do not load any third-party script until Didomi consent is granted. Gate all analytics, marketing, and tracking scripts behind Didomi callbacks.
139	- **Marketing opt-in:** Unchecked by default on all storefronts except US (pre-checked). Sync opt-in state: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys.
140	
141	_Per-storefront Didomi defaults, GTM/Enhanced Conversions setup, and Inside Chat rules: see [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md)._
142	
143	## Type Definitions
144	
145	- **Component-specific prop types:** co-locate at the top of the component file.
146	- **Shared types** (Commerce Cloud entities, API responses, shared hook signatures): `overrides/app/types/` — split into `commerce.ts`, `components.ts`, `hooks.ts`, re-exported via `index.ts`.
147	- Don't re-declare types already exported by `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` — import them directly.
148	
149	## Testing
150	
151	Three layers: **Vitest** (unit logic) · **Storybook** `play` (component interactions) · **Playwright** (E2E). Write tests only where failure would be non-obvious or costly to debug — data mapping, integration boundaries, complex state, and pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken. Every UI component needs a `.stories.tsx`; every logic-heavy feature needs a `.test.ts` or a story `play`.
152	
153	Full layer guidance, file layout, selector priority, and mocking policy: [.claude/rules/testing.md](.claude/rules/testing.md). (The no-MSW rule in Rules applies to production paths only.)
154	
155	## Graceful Degradation
156	
157	Each external system must fail independently — one outage must not break the whole page. Two defaults override any per-system behaviour: **fail closed on consent** (if consent state is unknown, load no third-party scripts), and **never silently substitute a different checkout, payment, or commerce flow** when an integration is down — surface an explicit error instead.
158	
159	## Performance
160	
161	Mobile page speed is a top priority. Every change that touches rendering, data fetching, or assets must not regress it.
162	
163	- **LCP budget is tight (≤ 2s at p75 mobile)** — Defer every third-party script that isn't required for first paint. Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM, Optimizely, Inside Chat, Narvar EDD, reCAPTCHA, etc.) must not block LCP — use `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection. If a new third-party integration looks like it might land on the critical path, flag it before merging.
164	- **Images:** Always use lazy loading and serve correctly sized images. Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
165	- **Code splitting:** Prefer dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on initial render.
166	- **Data fetching:** Avoid over-fetching — request only the fields you need. Waterfall requests are not acceptable; parallelise where possible.
167	- **Bundle size:** Do not introduce large dependencies without confirming with the user.
168	- **Dependencies:** Before implementing any feature that may require a third-party library, check `package.json` for what is already installed. Evaluate whether an existing dependency can satisfy the requirement. If a better third-party option exists, present the recommendation (existing vs. new, with trade-offs) and wait for user approval before installing anything.
169	
170	## Gotchas
171	
172	- **Theme runtime errors:** Custom components (e.g. `ListMenu`) must be defined in the theme object or destructuring will throw.
173	- **Commerce SDK types not importable:** Check `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` for generated definitions, or declare a narrow local `type`.
174	- **Magento password migration:** Passwords were not migrated from Magento — all existing customers must reset at go-live. Do not assume any saved credentials exist. Account creation and login flows must handle this gracefully (CFD-013).

176	## Requirements
177	
178	Requirements for this project are in `.docs/`, they must be strictly followed.
179	Before any code changes, verify logic against relevant `.docs/` files.

181	
182	If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or not yet confirmed — **stop, flag the ambiguity, propose a solution, and wait for user approval before proceeding.** Do not fill gaps with assumptions.
183	
184	Verification: Start every task by briefly stating which doc/section you are following (e.g. "Implementing per auth.md section 2.1" or "Implementing per 07-adyen.md §3").

186	**Doc integrity:** Confirmed PRDs (`.docs/prd/`) and finalised Figma designs are the source of truth for _requirements_. `.docs/integration/` docs are guides for _how_ each integration works technically. 189	
190	`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Read [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md) at the start of every session (or run `/session-start`).
