# Zimmermann - Salesforce PWA Kit (Production)

> **STRICT RULE — TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.**
> Every file created or modified under `overrides/` **must** use `.ts` or `.tsx`.
> `.js` and `.jsx` files are not acceptable here, including theme files, stories, and config modules.
> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`.

Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com, a luxury Australian fashion brand. Must be robust and secure and SEO-friendly. See [.docs/architecture.md](.docs/architecture.md) for stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths.

Tier classifications and protected-file lists live in [.claude/rules/](.claude/rules/) — loaded automatically per session. Custom slash commands for scaffolding and review live in [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/).

## Branch Rules

**At session start, always run `git branch --show-current`.** If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — do not make any changes.

| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       | Allowed?      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Primary working context for new work                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       | ✅ Yes        | Non-urgent bug fixes. Mechanically identical to `feature/*` — naming is for commit hygiene                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `release/*`               | `develop`              | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ⚠️ Supervised | Plan-first + confirm-every-edit required. Code logic fixes must use a `fix/release-*` sub-branch                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch, then forward-merged to `develop` once the release ships | ✅ Yes        | Only path for code logic fixes on a release. PR targets the release branch; SIT gate runs against the PR. Treated like `feature/*` on the sub-branch itself — the "Supervised" plan-first + confirm-every-edit rules apply only to direct edits on the `release/*` branch |
| `hotfix/*`                | `main`                 | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        | ✅ Yes        | Urgent production fixes only. Tier 1 rules still apply. Must be back-merged to `develop` to prevent drift                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `develop`                 | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `main`                    | —                      | —                                                                               | ❌ Never      | Human commits only                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

> **On `release/*` or `hotfix/*` branches you MUST read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) before any action.** It holds the supervised-edit rules (plan-first, confirm-every-edit, `fix/release-*` sub-branch flow) and the GitFlow back-merge rules that apply in addition to the Hard Rules below. On `feature/*` and `fix/*`, ignore it.

## Hard Rules

1. **Never operate on `develop` or `main`** branches.
2. **Never modify a Tier 1 file** without the developer explicitly naming it in the prompt and confirming owner approval — unless the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) applies. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md).
3. **Never modify `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`** — all design token changes go through the UI designer.
4. **Never modify `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, or `worker/main.js`.** These are absolute — the verified-session exception in [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) does not apply to them, regardless of approver status. `.github/workflows/` is Tier 1 CI/CD config and instead follows the standard Hard Rule #2 process (verified-session exception applies).
5. **Never refactor upward.** Fixing a bug in a component does not mean touching the hook or utility it calls.
6. **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.**
7. **Never add or remove packages** from `package.json` without integration team approval. When approved, always use `npm install` rather than editing `package.json` directly.
8. **Never modify test configuration files** (`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `tests/lighthouserc.js`).
9. **Never delete files** without being explicitly asked in the current prompt. You may propose deletion and let a human confirm.
10. **Never touch more than one protection tier** in a single change without stopping to confirm scope with the developer.
11. **Never assume a hook is safe to modify** because it has a simple name — check the frozenFiles list first.
12. **When requirements are unclear, ask one clarifying question at a time.** Do not proceed with assumptions and do not batch questions. Wait for the answer before asking the next question or writing any code.
13. **Never use `--dangerously-skip-permissions`** on `release/**`, `main`, or `develop`. This flag bypasses all edit confirmations and is only permitted in CI automation contexts, never in interactive developer sessions on shared or protected branches.
14. **Never reference code from a later sprint.** Check [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) before scoping any new work. If a task depends on a component, hook, or integration that belongs to a later sprint, stop and ask whether to build a placeholder or whether that sprint is already complete.
15. **Never create a git commit, push to remote, or open/close a PR** without the developer explicitly requesting it in the current prompt. Resuming from a session summary, a task list, or a "natural next step" is not an instruction to commit — wait for an explicit ask.

## Tier 1 Approval — How It's Actually Enforced

Claude Code's confirmation prompt before touching a Tier 1 file (Hard Rule #2) is a workflow
safeguard, not the security boundary — it can't be, since it only governs what Claude itself
does, not what any other tool or a direct `git push` can do. The real enforcement is server-side:

- [CODEOWNERS](../CODEOWNERS) routes every Tier 1 path to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`, a
  real GitHub org team.
- Branch protection on `develop`/`main`/`release/**` requires an approving code-owner review
  before merge — this is the actual gate, enforced natively by GitHub with no Actions
  involvement, so it can't be affected by a broken or delayed CI run.
- `.github/workflows/protected-file-guard.yml`'s `tier1-guard` job posts a loud warning and an
  owner-contact-map on any PR touching a Tier 1 path. It is **not** a required status check —
  GitHub locked down cross-run check-run updates in Feb 2025, which made a "hard-fail until
  approved, then flip to pass on review" required check impossible to implement reliably (a
  fresh commit is needed to re-evaluate it, since a later review can't flip an earlier run's
  result). The CODEOWNERS-based review requirement above is the real, working block.

Because the actual gate lives in GitHub, not in Claude's judgement, this file does not encode
personal names or email addresses as a bypass condition — a string in a shared, version-controlled
file is not an identity check; anyone (or any other Claude session) could satisfy it by typing it.
Instead, Claude may verify the real, authenticated identity behind the current session:

- Before pausing to ask for Tier 1 confirmation, run `gh api user --jq .login`, then check
  `gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members --jq '.[].login'` (or check for `admin`
  via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/collaborators/<login>/permission`). If that GitHub
  login is a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or holds repo admin, Claude may proceed
  with the edit after stating which Tier 1 file is being touched and why — no separate
  confirmation message is required, since GitHub already recognises that account as an approver.
- If the authenticated login is **not** a member/admin, Claude must still stop per Hard Rule #2:
  name the file, and require the developer to secure an approving review from
  `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` before the PR can merge. CODEOWNERS auto-requests that review
  and branch protection blocks the merge without it, regardless of what `tier1-guard` reports.
- This check only ever reduces _how many times Claude pauses to ask_. It changes nothing about
  what GitHub will actually allow to merge — that's deliberate, so a compromised or careless
  Claude session can't grant itself write access to a frozen file.

## Coding Task Workflow

Every coding task follows these four steps in order. Do not skip ahead — pause at the marked points and wait for the user.

1. **Clarify requirements.** Identify every gap, ambiguity, or contradiction in the request and the relevant `.docs/`. Confirm each one with the user before moving on — no assumptions. See Hard Rule #12: ask one question at a time.
2. **Plan.** State the files you intend to touch, _why_ each one is being touched, and any base template files that will need to be copied to `overrides/`. Then **pause** and wait for the user to confirm the plan. See the **Minimal changes** rule below.
3. **Copy first (if any).** For every base template file identified in step 2, follow the **Copy-first rule** in the Rules section. Then **pause** and let the user test and stage the override files before any functional changes.
4. **Implement.** Make the planned modifications. Remove the `console.log` markers from step 3 once the user confirms the overrides are rendering. Before committing a non-trivial code change, run a local CodeRabbit review: confirm the CLI is installed and authenticated (`coderabbit auth status`; if not authenticated, `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` — see `.env.sample`), then `cr review --light --base develop` (use `main` instead on a `release/**`/`hotfix/**` branch). **The CLI is required, not optional** — if it isn't installed or authenticated, stop and have the developer install it (https://www.coderabbit.ai/cli) and run `npm run env -- init` to pull the shared key, rather than committing without a local review. The review itself is still advisory relative to the actual merge gate (the GitHub PR review remains the real gate) — use judgement on whether a flagged finding is worth fixing before the commit vs. leaving it for the PR review to catch, but the review must actually run.

**Responding to a CodeRabbit PR review.** Once CodeRabbit finishes reviewing an open PR, always leave an explicit in-thread reply for every finding, whether it's fixed or not — CodeRabbit's learning feature picks up patterns from PR conversation, so silence teaches it nothing and an explanation teaches it to stop flagging the same non-issue. A fix commit alone, with no reply posted on the thread, doesn't count. For a finding that gets fixed, a short in-thread reply confirming the fix (referencing the commit is fine) is enough. For a finding that is *not* being fixed because it conflicts with this repo's own rules/docs/architecture (e.g. a Tier 1 exception that was actually followed correctly, an intentional design tradeoff already recorded in `.docs/`) — reply in-thread explaining the specific rule or doc that justifies not changing it, so CodeRabbit's learning has the context to recognise the same pattern next time instead of re-flagging it. Never silently dismiss a finding without a reply.

## When to Stop and Ask a Human

| Trigger                                                                      | Action                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Task requires a Tier 1 file                                                  | Check the authenticated `gh` identity against `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`/admin (see [Tier 1 Approval](#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced)). If verified, name the file and proceed. Otherwise stop and require named owner approval. |
| A shared hook needs its function signature changed                           | Stop. Requires a team RFC.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| A new package dependency is needed                                           | Stop. Integration team must approve.                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Current branch is `develop` or `main`                                        | Stop immediately. No changes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Change affects more than one regional site config                            | Stop. Integration team sign-off required.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Change spans multiple protection tiers                                       | Stop. Confirm scope with the developer before continuing.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Requirement is missing, ambiguous, contradictory, or unconfirmed in `.docs/` | Stop. Flag, propose, wait for approval (see Requirements section).                                                                                                                                                                                  |

## Multi-site & Routing

The SFCC sites are hard routing and config boundaries — **never bleed config across sites.** Never assume a storefront's routing, URL prefix, checkout ownership, or consent defaults without checking [.docs/prd/regional.md](.docs/prd/regional.md).

Two defaults override any per-system behaviour: **fail closed on consent** (if consent state is unknown, load no third-party scripts), and **never silently substitute a different checkout, payment, or commerce flow** when an integration is down — surface an explicit error instead.

## Performance

Mobile page speed is a top priority. Every change that touches rendering, data fetching, or assets must not regress it.

- **LCP budget is tight (≤ 2s at p75 mobile)** — Defer every third-party script that isn't required for first paint. Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM, Optimizely, Inside Chat, Narvar EDD, reCAPTCHA, etc.) must not block LCP — use `defer`, `async`, or post-hydration injection. If a new third-party integration looks like it might land on the critical path, flag it before merging.
- **Images:** Always use lazy loading and serve correctly sized images. Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
- **Code splitting:** Prefer dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on initial render.
- **Data fetching:** Avoid over-fetching — request only the fields you need. Waterfall requests are not acceptable; parallelise where possible.
- **Bundle size:** Do not introduce large dependencies without confirming with the user.
- **Dependencies:** Before implementing any feature that may require a third-party library, check `package.json` for what is already installed. Evaluate whether an existing dependency can satisfy the requirement. If a better third-party option exists, present the recommendation (existing vs. new, with trade-offs) and wait for user approval before installing anything.

## Gotchas

- **Theme runtime errors:** Custom components (e.g. `ListMenu`) must be defined in the theme object or destructuring will throw.
- **Commerce SDK types not importable:** Check `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` for generated definitions, or declare a narrow local `type`.
- **Magento password migration:** Passwords were not migrated from Magento — all existing customers must reset at go-live. Do not assume any saved credentials exist. Account creation and login flows must handle this gracefully (CFD-013).

## Requirements

Requirements for this project are in `.docs/`, they must be strictly followed.
Before any code changes, verify logic against relevant `.docs/` files.
For any task that touches an external integration, check the matching `.docs/integration/NN-*.md` doc.

If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or not yet confirmed — **stop, flag the ambiguity, propose a solution, and wait for user approval before proceeding.** Do not fill gaps with assumptions.

Verification: Start every task by briefly stating which doc/section you are following (e.g. "Implementing per auth.md section 2.1" or "Implementing per 07-adyen.md §3").

**Doc integrity:** Confirmed PRDs (`.docs/prd/`) and finalised Figma designs are the source of truth for _requirements_. `.docs/integration/` docs are guides for _how_ each integration works technically. If a user instruction contradicts either, pause immediately — cite the specific doc, section, and requirement ID — and ask the user whether the doc should be updated or the instruction is a deliberate override. Do not proceed silently either way. The same applies if you spot any improvement or conflict within the docs themselves.

## Living Memory

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Read [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md) at the start of every session (or run `/session-start`). For what belongs in each memory file and when to update it, see the [session-start skill](.claude/skills/session-start/SKILL.md).

**Open items that block implementation** are listed under "Unresolved Dependencies" in [.docs/memory/projectState.md](.docs/memory/projectState.md). Ask the user before hard-coding assumptions about any of them.

1	# Tagging & Environment Promotion
2	
3	How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
4	day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
5	supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
6	this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Tag taxonomy
11	
12	Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. The **tag-promoted** tiers
13	(`test` / `uat` / `staging` / `prod`) deploy a specific tag — never "whatever's on a branch right
14	now." (The continuous tiers are the exception: `dev` and `sit` deploy commit refs, and Test also
15	takes a branch ref for on-demand quick looks — see the Environment model below.)
16	
17	| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
18	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
19	| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
20	| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
21	| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |
22	
23	**Versioning:**
24	- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
25	  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
26	- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
27	  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
28	- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
29	  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
30	- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — it counts
31	  candidate builds, not deployments. The same `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be deployed (and re-deployed) to
32	  Test on demand; which environment ran which candidate is tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions
33	  run history, not the tag name.
34	- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
35	  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
36	  relies on.
37	
38	Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
39	rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.
40	
41	---
42	
43	## Cutting a tag
44	
45	Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
46	deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
47	and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
48	(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
49	push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
50	bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.
51	
52	**Release candidate (any developer):**
53	
54	```bash
55	git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull --ff-only   # fail rather than tag a local merge commit
56	git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
57	git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
58	gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
59	```
60	
61	- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
62	  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
63	- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.
64	
65	**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
66	`main`, then promote it up through `uat` → `staging` → `prod`. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
67	at this point to produce the GitHub Release.
68	
69	**Rollback.** The downgrade guard (see below) deliberately blocks deploying an older tag, so a
70	rollback takes one of two authorised paths:
71	
72	- **Emergency (fastest) — re-activate the previous bundle in Managed Runtime**, outside the deploy
73	  pipeline (the rollback procedure in the Environment Topology doc). This does not run the guard, so
74	  afterwards re-record the baseline so it doesn't treat a superseded tag as live:
75	  `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record prod v0.1.0`.
76	- **Controlled — pipeline rollback with the guard override.** Redeploy the known-good tag with
77	  `rollback=true`; the guard's downgrade check is skipped (the run logs the skip for audit) and
78	  `record` still runs, so the rolled-back tag becomes the new live baseline:
79	  `gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.1.0 -f rollback=true`. Because this bypasses the guard,
80	  its only human gate is the environment's **required reviewers** — so `prod` (and `staging`/`uat`)
81	  must have required reviewers with "prevent self-review" configured. **Prerequisite: until that is
82	  set, `rollback=true` is not gated.**
83	
84	---
85	
86	## Enforcement — what actually holds the line
87	
88	On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
89	Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
90	ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
91	order of reliability:
92	
93	1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
94	   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
95	   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
96	   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
97	   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
98	2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
99	   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
100	3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
101	   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
102	   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
103	   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
104	   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.
105	
106	GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
107	live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
108	renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.
109	
110	---
111	
112	## Environment model — two categories
113	
114	| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
115	| --- | --- | --- |
116	| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
117	| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |
118	
119	**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
120	unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
121	continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
122	tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
123	visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.
124	
125	**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
126	prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
127	`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).
128	
129	---
130	
131	## Downgrade protection (version-guard)
132	
133	[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
134	`deploy-*.yml` workflows:
135	
136	- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
137	  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
138	  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
139	- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
140	  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
141	  we record it ourselves and read it back).
142	- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
143	  two-category model above).
144	- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).
145	
146	---
147	
148	## The Test gate
149	
150	`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
151	quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
152	**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.
153	
154	- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
155	  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
156	  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
157	- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
158	  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.
159	
160	This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
161	pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.
162	
163	---
164	
165	## References
166	
167	- Design: Confluence *Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)* (335216656)

# Tagging & Environment Promotion

How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

---

## Tag taxonomy

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. The **tag-promoted** tiers
(`test` / `uat` / `staging` / `prod`) deploy a specific tag — never "whatever's on a branch right
now." (The continuous tiers are the exception: `dev` and `sit` deploy commit refs, and Test also
takes a branch ref for on-demand quick looks — see the Environment model below.)

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — it counts
  candidate builds, not deployments. The same `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be deployed (and re-deployed) to
  Test on demand; which environment ran which candidate is tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions
  run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.

**Release candidate (any developer):**

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull --ff-only   # fail rather than tag a local merge commit
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.

**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
`main`, then promote it up through `uat` → `staging` → `prod`. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
at this point to produce the GitHub Release.

**Rollback.** The downgrade guard (see below) deliberately blocks deploying an older tag, so a
rollback takes one of two authorised paths:

- **Emergency (fastest) — re-activate the previous bundle in Managed Runtime**, outside the deploy
  pipeline (the rollback procedure in the Environment Topology doc). This does not run the guard, so
  afterwards re-record the baseline so it doesn't treat a superseded tag as live:
  `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record prod v0.1.0`.
- **Controlled — pipeline rollback with the guard override.** Redeploy the known-good tag with
  `rollback=true`; the guard's downgrade check is skipped (the run logs the skip for audit) and
  `record` still runs, so the rolled-back tag becomes the new live baseline:
  `gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.1.0 -f rollback=true`. Because this bypasses the guard,
  its only human gate is the environment's **required reviewers** — so `prod` (and `staging`/`uat`)
  must have required reviewers with "prevent self-review" configured. **Prerequisite: until that is
  set, `rollback=true` is not gated.**

---

## Enforcement — what actually holds the line

On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
order of reliability:

1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.

GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.

---

## Environment model — two categories

| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.

---

## References

- Design: Confluence *Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)* (335216656)
- Branch rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) · supervised release: [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md)
- Implementation: [versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs) · [deploy-*.yml](../../.github/workflows/) · [tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml) · pre-push hook
- Changelog: [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)

---

1	name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)
2	
3	# SFCC-751 develop-PR path, split out of qa.yml's e2e-browserstack
4	# (2026-08-25 cost review). Per-story Zephyr-linked BrowserStack execution
5	# against a develop-targeted PR's own ephemeral MRT preview
6	# (deploy-preview.yml), triggered the instant that preview finishes
7	# building instead of polling for it from an already-running, already-
8	# billed job. The old design started in parallel with Deploy Preview and
9	# slept in a loop waiting for it — up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner
10	# time per push. workflow_run fires exactly once, exactly when Deploy
11	# Preview completes, with everything this job needs already in the event
12	# payload or a downloadable artifact — no polling, so no billed wait.
13	#
14	# release/** PRs are unaffected — deploy-preview.yml never runs for
15	# fix/release-* branches, so this workflow never fires for them; they keep
16	# using qa.yml's e2e-browserstack (full suite, static test tier, no wait).
17	#
18	# GitHub only evaluates a workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition
19	# from the repository's default branch — this file is invisible to Actions
20	# entirely until merged to develop, and (like zephyr-results-sync.yml) can
21	# never be dry-run against a real PR pre-merge. See testing.md's note on
22	# zephyr-results-sync.yml for the same caveat.
23	on:
24	  workflow_run:
25	    workflows: ['Deploy Preview']
26	    types: [completed]
27	
28	permissions:
29	  contents: read
30	  actions: read # to download artifacts from the triggering Deploy Preview run and look up its matching QA run
31	  pull-requests: read # to find the open PR for this branch
32	
33	jobs:
34	  e2e-browserstack:
35	    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
36	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
37	    # A cancelled Deploy Preview run skips this job entirely (there's
38	    # nothing to test and no hostname artifact could exist). Any other
39	    # conclusion still runs -- if Deploy Preview failed rather than
40	    # succeeded, "Resolve BrowserStack test target" below fails the job
41	    # loudly instead of silently testing an unrelated environment (see
42	    # that step's own comment for why the old test-tier fallback was
43	    # removed, CodeRabbit, 2026-08-26).
44	    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
45	    timeout-minutes: 25
46	    environment: test # for the E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets
47	    steps:
48	      # Checked out at the triggering run's own head_sha, not the default
49	      # branch — this job needs to execute the PR's own e2e specs and
50	      # scripts/computeBuildName.mjs, not develop's copy of them (unlike
51	      # zephyr-results-sync.yml, which deliberately checks out develop for
52	      # a script-trust reason that doesn't apply here — see that
53	      # workflow's comment). This carries the same secrets-exposure shape
54	      # qa.yml's old pull_request-triggered e2e-browserstack job already
55	      # had: real BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_* secrets alongside PR-branch code.
56	      # Acceptable under this repo's branch model (feature/fix branches
57	      # only, never a fork — see AGENTS.md > Branch Rules); would need
58	      # re-review if fork-based PRs are ever introduced.
59	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
60	        with:
61	          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
62	
63	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
64	        with:
65	          node-version: '24'
66	          cache: 'npm'
67	
68	      # --ignore-scripts, not --include=dev with lifecycle scripts enabled:
69	      # this job checks out and executes a PR branch's own code with real
70	      # BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_*/E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets in scope, and
71	      # workflow_run grants those secrets unconditionally -- unlike
72	      # pull_request, there is no pending-approval gate here even for a
73	      # same-repo branch. Without --ignore-scripts, anyone with push access
74	      # to a feature/fix branch could add a preinstall/postinstall script
75	      # to exfiltrate every secret this job can see, with no review step
76	      # in between (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-26). Skipping
77	      # lifecycle scripts is safe here: this job never builds or runs the
78	      # app locally (it only drives Playwright against an already-deployed
79	      # preview), so it doesn't need postinstall's translation-compilation
80	      # or registry-generation side effects.
81	      - name: Install dependencies
82	        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
83	
84	      # Single API call, no loop — by the time Deploy Preview has finished
85	      # (~5-10 min after push), the PR this branch belongs to has existed
86	      # for the whole run, so there's nothing to wait for here either.
87	      - name: Find open PR for this branch
88	        id: pr
89	        env:
90	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
91	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
92	        run: |
93	          PR_JSON=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open \
94	            --json number,title,body,baseRefName --jq '.[0] // empty')
95	          if [[ -z "$PR_JSON" ]]; then
96	            echo "No open PR found for branch $BRANCH -- nothing to test."
97	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
98	            exit 0
99	          fi
100	          BASE=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.baseRefName')
101	          if [[ "$BASE" != "develop" ]]; then
102	            # deploy-preview.yml only triggers on feature/**, fix/** pushes,
103	            # which per AGENTS.md > Branch Rules always target develop — this
104	            # is a defensive check, not an expected path.
105	            echo "PR #$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number') targets $BASE, not develop -- skipping."
106	            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
107	            exit 0
108	          fi
109	          echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
110	          echo "number=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
111	          # Title/body go to files, not GITHUB_OUTPUT -- both are
112	          # attacker-controllable free text and could contain newlines or
113	          # break a later env: interpolation otherwise.
114	          echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.title' > pr-title.txt
115	          echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.body // ""' > pr-body.txt
116	
117	      # Same regex/signal as qa.yml's detect-changes "Detect Jira story
118	      # keys" step. Duplicated rather than shared across workflows -- small
119	      # and self-contained, and this workflow has no other dependency on
120	      # qa.yml's run. No key found -> nothing to scope a per-story
121	      # BrowserStack/Zephyr run to, so skip (mirrors the old "job doesn't
122	      # run at all" behaviour, not a fallback-to-full).
123	      - name: Detect Jira story keys
124	        id: jira
125	        if: steps.pr.outputs.skip == 'false'
126	        env:
127	          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
128	        run: |
129	          KEYS=$( { cat pr-title.txt pr-body.txt; printf '%s\n' "$BRANCH"; } \
130	            | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
131	          echo "keys=$KEYS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack Preview)

# SFCC-751 develop-PR path, split out of qa.yml's e2e-browserstack
# (2026-08-25 cost review). Per-story Zephyr-linked BrowserStack execution
# against a develop-targeted PR's own ephemeral MRT preview
# (deploy-preview.yml), triggered the instant that preview finishes
# building instead of polling for it from an already-running, already-
# billed job. The old design started in parallel with Deploy Preview and
# slept in a loop waiting for it — up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner
# time per push. workflow_run fires exactly once, exactly when Deploy
# Preview completes, with everything this job needs already in the event
# payload or a downloadable artifact — no polling, so no billed wait.
#
# release/** PRs are unaffected — deploy-preview.yml never runs for
# fix/release-* branches, so this workflow never fires for them; they keep
# using qa.yml's e2e-browserstack (full suite, static test tier, no wait).
#
# GitHub only evaluates a workflow_run-triggering workflow's own definition
# from the repository's default branch — this file is invisible to Actions
# entirely until merged to develop, and (like zephyr-results-sync.yml) can
# never be dry-run against a real PR pre-merge. See testing.md's note on
# zephyr-results-sync.yml for the same caveat.
on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Deploy Preview']
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  contents: read
  actions: read # to download artifacts from the triggering Deploy Preview run and look up its matching QA run
  pull-requests: read # to find the open PR for this branch

jobs:
  e2e-browserstack:
    name: Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # A cancelled Deploy Preview run skips this job entirely (there's
    # nothing to test and no hostname artifact could exist). Any other
    # conclusion still runs -- if Deploy Preview failed rather than
    # succeeded, "Resolve BrowserStack test target" below fails the job
    # loudly instead of silently testing an unrelated environment (see
    # that step's own comment for why the old test-tier fallback was
    # removed, CodeRabbit, 2026-08-26).
    if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    environment: test # for the E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets
    steps:
      # Checked out at the triggering run's own head_sha, not the default
      # branch — this job needs to execute the PR's own e2e specs and
      # scripts/computeBuildName.mjs, not develop's copy of them (unlike
      # zephyr-results-sync.yml, which deliberately checks out develop for
      # a script-trust reason that doesn't apply here — see that
      # workflow's comment). This carries the same secrets-exposure shape
      # qa.yml's old pull_request-triggered e2e-browserstack job already
      # had: real BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_* secrets alongside PR-branch code.
      # Acceptable under this repo's branch model (feature/fix branches
      # only, never a fork — see AGENTS.md > Branch Rules); would need
      # re-review if fork-based PRs are ever introduced.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      # --ignore-scripts, not --include=dev with lifecycle scripts enabled:
      # this job checks out and executes a PR branch's own code with real
      # BROWSERSTACK_*/JIRA_*/E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_* secrets in scope, and
      # workflow_run grants those secrets unconditionally -- unlike
      # pull_request, there is no pending-approval gate here even for a
      # same-repo branch. Without --ignore-scripts, anyone with push access
      # to a feature/fix branch could add a preinstall/postinstall script
      # to exfiltrate every secret this job can see, with no review step
      # in between (CodeRabbit flagged this correctly, 2026-08-26). Skipping
      # lifecycle scripts is safe here: this job never builds or runs the
      # app locally (it only drives Playwright against an already-deployed
      # preview), so it doesn't need postinstall's translation-compilation
      # or registry-generation side effects.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Single API call, no loop — by the time Deploy Preview has finished
      # (~5-10 min after push), the PR this branch belongs to has existed
      # for the whole run, so there's nothing to wait for here either.
      - name: Find open PR for this branch
        id: pr
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
        run: |
          PR_JSON=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open \
            --json number,title,body,baseRefName --jq '.[0] // empty')
          if [[ -z "$PR_JSON" ]]; then
            echo "No open PR found for branch $BRANCH -- nothing to test."
            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          BASE=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.baseRefName')
          if [[ "$BASE" != "develop" ]]; then
            # deploy-preview.yml only triggers on feature/**, fix/** pushes,
            # which per AGENTS.md > Branch Rules always target develop — this
            # is a defensive check, not an expected path.
            echo "PR #$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number') targets $BASE, not develop -- skipping."
            echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "skip=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "number=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.number')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Title/body go to files, not GITHUB_OUTPUT -- both are
          # attacker-controllable free text and could contain newlines or
          # break a later env: interpolation otherwise.
          echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.title' > pr-title.txt
          echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.body // ""' > pr-body.txt

      # Same regex/signal as qa.yml's detect-changes "Detect Jira story
      # keys" step. Duplicated rather than shared across workflows -- small
      # and self-contained, and this workflow has no other dependency on
      # qa.yml's run. No key found -> nothing to scope a per-story
      # BrowserStack/Zephyr run to, so skip (mirrors the old "job doesn't
      # run at all" behaviour, not a fallback-to-full).
      - name: Detect Jira story keys
        id: jira
        if: steps.pr.outputs.skip == 'false'
        env:
          BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
        run: |
          KEYS=$( { cat pr-title.txt pr-body.txt; printf '%s\n' "$BRANCH"; } \
            | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
          echo "keys=$KEYS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Single-shot lookup of the QA run for this same commit -- no loop.
      # detect-changes (qa.yml) finishes in well under a minute; Deploy
      # Preview takes several minutes minimum, so by the time this job
      # starts, that artifact is essentially guaranteed to already exist.
      # If the lookup or download comes up empty for any reason, fail open
      # (assume e2e-relevant) rather than adding a retry loop to chase an
      # optimisation -- worst case this runs BrowserStack once when
      # detect-changes would have skipped it, not a correctness problem.
      - name: Look up matching QA run
        id: qa-run
        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        run: |
          RUN_ID=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/workflows/qa.yml/runs?head_sha=$HEAD_SHA" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].id // empty')
          echo "run_id=$RUN_ID" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Download e2e-relevance artifact
        id: download-e2e-scope
        if: steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: e2e-scope
          run-id: ${{ steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      - name: Check e2e relevance
        id: relevance
        if: steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''
        run: |
          if [[ -f e2e-scope.json ]] && [[ "$(jq -r '.e2e' e2e-scope.json)" == "false" ]]; then
            echo "Nothing e2e-relevant changed on this commit (per qa.yml's detect-changes) -- skipping BrowserStack."
            echo "relevant=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "relevant=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Compute build name
        id: build-name
        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
        run: |
          PRIMARY_KEY=$(echo "${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}" | awk '{print $1}')
          NAME=$(node scripts/computeBuildName.mjs "$PRIMARY_KEY")
          echo "name=$NAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        env:
          JIRA_URL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_URL }}
          JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_EMAIL }}
          JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.JIRA_AUTOMATION_API_TOKEN }}

      # zephyr-results-sync.yml downloads this rather than recomputing it
      # -- see that workflow's own comment for the drift reason.
      - name: Persist build name for the Zephyr sync job
        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
        run: printf '%s\n' "$BUILD_NAME" > browserstack-build-name.txt

      - name: Upload build name artifact
        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: browserstack-build-name
          path: browserstack-build-name.txt
          retention-days: 7

      # Deploy Preview persists this as an artifact on its own run only
      # after a successful build+push (see that workflow's own comment) --
      # a missing artifact here means either that run didn't reach that
      # step, or it failed outright.
      - name: Download preview hostname artifact
        id: download-preview-hostname
        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: mrt-preview-hostname
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}

      # No fallback to the static test tier here (removed 2026-08-26,
      # CodeRabbit flagged this correctly). This job's whole reason to
      # exist is testing THIS PR's own code -- silently substituting the
      # static test tier (an unrelated, tag-promoted environment with no
      # guaranteed relationship to any given PR, per tagging.md) when the
      # preview isn't available would let a develop PR whose deployment
      # genuinely failed still produce a green, story-tagged Zephyr
      # execution and closed Jira defect that prove nothing about the
      # PR's own changes. Same principle AGENTS.md's Graceful Degradation
      # section states for checkout/payment: never silently substitute a
      # different flow, surface an explicit error instead.
      - name: Resolve BrowserStack test target
        id: resolve-target
        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
        run: |
          if [[ -f preview-hostname.txt ]]; then
            HOSTNAME=$(cat preview-hostname.txt)
            echo "Testing this PR's own MRT preview: https://$HOSTNAME"
            echo "retail_app_home=https://$HOSTNAME" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "::error::Deploy Preview produced no mrt-preview-hostname artifact for this run (conclusion: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}). Refusing to run story-tagged BrowserStack tests against the static test tier -- that would attribute a Zephyr execution and possible auto-filed Jira defect to code that was never actually deployed for this PR. Investigate the Deploy Preview run for commit ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}."
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Run Zimmermann e2e on BrowserStack
        if: steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'
        run: |
          GREP=$(echo "$KEYS" | tr ' ' '\n' | sed 's/^/@/' | paste -sd '|')
          npx browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep "$GREP"
        env:
          KEYS: ${{ steps.jira.outputs.keys }}
          BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME }}
          BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY }}
          SPRINT_NUMBER: ${{ steps.build-name.outputs.name }}
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ steps.resolve-target.outputs.retail_app_home }}
          # Sent regardless of which target was resolved above. The `test`
          # tier is access-gated (confirmed with the developer, 2026-08-25)
          # -- without this header every request is rejected before the
          # page can load. Whether the PR's own MRT preview target also
          # needs it is unconfirmed, but sending an extra header a target
          # doesn't require is harmless. See BasePage.js's
          # applyExtraHeaders() and testing.md > Access-gated preview URLs.
          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME }}
          E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE: ${{ secrets.E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE }}
          PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL }}
          PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD }}
          E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU: ${{ secrets.E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU }}
          E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER: ${{ secrets.E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER }}
          SITE_ID: au  # Default — parameterise for multi-region runs

111:- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. ### 13.4 Selector priority

Tests select elements the way users and assistive tech perceive them: accessible selectors (role + name, label, visible text) first, semantic HTML attributes second (`alt`, `title`), `data-testid` only when nothing semantic applies. Tag/class/DOM-position selectors are not used. This doubles as a continuous accessibility check.

---

## 14. CI/CD & Environments

This section probably belong to a DevOps TSD, but will put here temporarily until we have one.

### 14.1 Topology

A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| #   | Tier            | Owner         | Purpose                                                                      | Third-party availability                                              | Deploy trigger                                                              |
| --- | --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Local**       | Digital       | Feature build on developer machines                                          | All services mocked (MSW stubs)                                       | `npm start`                                                                 |
| 2   | **Dev**         | Digital       | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop`                                                          |
| 3   | **SIT**         | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence                               | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test                  | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4   | **UAT**         | Shared        | Business acceptance across all 6 regions                                     | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox                 | Business approval gate                                                      |
| 5   | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared        | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows    | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox  | Booked 2-week window                                                        |
| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |

Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

### 14.2 Branch model

GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.

| Branch                    | Branched from          | Merges to                                                                       |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `feature/*`               | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       |
| `fix/*`                   | `develop`              | `develop`                                                                       |
| `release/*`               | `develop`              | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
| `hotfix/*`                | `main`                 | `main` **and** `develop`                                                        |
| `develop`, `main`         | —                      | protected; PR-only                                                              |

Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.

### 14.3 CI workflows

**QA workflow (`qa.yml`)** — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:

- Unit tests (Vitest)
- Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)

**SIT gate (`digital-sit.yml`)** — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:

- Playwright `p0` priority specs
- Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
- Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
- Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
- Trend gate against the LHCI history server

### 14.4 Deployment

Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:

- **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
- **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
- **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
- **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
- **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions

Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through UAT and Stage.

MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`.

# Environment Strategy, Branching & SIT Pipeline — Claude Code Briefing

## Programme Context

Zimmermann is migrating from Magento 2 to Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) using the PWA Kit
(`template-retail-react-app`) as the storefront baseline, deployed on Managed Runtime (MRT).

Seven storefronts are in scope: AU, UK, US domestic, US international (Global-e), EU domestic,
EU international (Global-e), and ME. The Digital pipeline must support all six active SFCC
storefronts simultaneously. NewStore (OMS) runs a parallel SIT cycle on its own cadence and
converges with Digital only at the STAGE tier.

Zimmermann has 20 SFCC sandboxes available and no MRT environment licence restriction.
This enables a clean six-tier topology with no shared-environment contention.

---

## Environment Topology — Six Tiers

```
LOCAL  →  DEV  →  SIT (parallel)  →  STAGE  →  UAT  →  PROD
```

### Tier 1 — LOCAL

| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC BM | n/a | Not used locally |
| MRT / PWA | `npm start` (developer machine only — no MRT deployment) | Feature development and local SSR testing |
| 3P systems | All stubs via MSW | No real third-party calls at this tier |
| OMS SIT | Not in scope | NewStore not involved at this tier |

**Who deploys here:** Individual developers run `npm start` locally. No MRT deployment for `feature/*` branches.

**CDN / cache:** n/a — local dev server only.

**Logging:** `debug` level. Source maps exposed.

---

### Tier 2 — DEV (Digital Dev)

| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC BM | SFCC STG org | Jobs: AP21 feed, OCI sync, Lengow |
| MRT / PWA | MRT staging | 7 storefronts, Playwright matrix, Lighthouse CI |
| 3P systems | MuleSoft STG only | All other third parties stubbed via MSW |
| OMS SIT | Not in scope | NewStore not involved at this tier |

**Who deploys here:** CI pipeline on every merge to `develop`. Auto-deployed.

**Gate:** `Digital SIT Gate` — composite GitHub Actions required status check. All four signals
must be green before promotion to STAGE is permitted:
- Playwright P0: 100% pass rate across 6 storefront configs
- Lighthouse CI: Performance ≥ 80, Accessibility ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90
- MuleSoft contract tests: no schema breach
- Bundle size: main.js < 180 kB, vendor.js < 250 kB, main.css < 50 kB

Vitest and Storybook interaction + a11y tests run in `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`) — they gate
the PR merge, not the environment deploy.

**CDN / cache:** 60s page TTL, 1h asset TTL.

100	| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |

### External services

Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Contentful Studio CMS, Global-e (international checkout + server-side pricing/catalogue feed — PRC-34..43 sign-off pending), Didomi (consent), GTM hosted on Addingwell (data layer + downstream tag loading via Tell No Lies). Full integration map below.

## Environments

Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| #   | Tier            | Owner         | Purpose                                                                      | Third-party availability                                              | Deploy trigger                                                              |
| --- | --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | **Local**       | Digital       | Feature build on developer machines                                          | All services mocked (MSW stubs)                                       | `npm start`                                                                 |
| 2   | **Dev**         | Digital       | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop`                                                          |
| 3   | **SIT**         | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence                               | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test                  | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4   | **UAT**         | Shared        | Business acceptance across all 6 regions                                     | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox                 | Business approval gate                                                      |
| 5   | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared        | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows    | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox  | Booked 2-week window                                                        |
| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |

**Stage** is the contractual performance-test environment referenced under [Pre-Build Decisions #3](#3--performance-budgets-) — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

**QA workflow** ([`qa.yml`](../.github/workflows/qa.yml)) runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`: Vitest unit tests and Storybook interaction + `@storybook/addon-a11y` component-level accessibility checks (`storybook test --ci`), in parallel. Code-correctness checks that run before any environment is involved.

**SIT gate** ([`digital-sit.yml`](../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)) runs on push/PR to `release/**`: Playwright `p0` specs, bundle-size check, MuleSoft contract tests, Lighthouse CI thresholds, LHCI trend gate. Environment-dependent checks against the deployed Dev tier. On merge to `develop` it also deploys to Dev. Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through UAT and Stage.

**MRT targets** in [mobify.config.js](../mobify.config.js) map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`. `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (`local | dev | sit | uat | stage | prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry, New Relic, and GTM.

## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)

Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.

## Overrides Pattern

1	# ── Environment switching ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2	# This file is the documented template for every variable the project uses. Each
3	# active line below is preceded by its own `# scope:shared`, `# scope:tier`,
4	# `# scope:personal`, or `# scope:auto` comment line (parsed by
5	# scripts/switchEnv.mjs, ignored by everything else — kept on its own line,
6	# not trailing on the KEY=value line, so a blank placeholder here still reads
7	# as genuinely empty to the pre-commit secret guard):
8	#   scope:shared   — same value across all 6 tiers (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod)
9	#                    AND same for the whole team. Lives in .env.shared; included
10	#                    in `push`/`init`'s pull to/from GitHub Environments.
11	#   scope:tier     — differs per tier. Lives in the gitignored .env.<tier> for
12	#                    whichever tier you're pointing local dev at; also
13	#                    included in `push`/pull.
14	#   scope:personal — tier-independent like shared, but a PERSONAL credential
15	#                    (your own Atlassian token, your own Contentful CMA token)
16	#                    that must never be centralized — still lives in
17	#                    .env.shared, but `push`/`init`'s pull skip it entirely.
18	#                    Each developer fills this in themselves.
19	#   scope:auto     — never hand-set; scripts/switchEnv.mjs injects this itself.
20	#
21	# A second optional tag `# mrt:true` marks variables that belong in the MRT
22	# Managed Runtime environment (storefront runtime config). Only keys tagged
23	# `mrt:true` are synced by the "Sync Env Vars to MRT" GitHub Actions workflow.
24	# CI/tooling vars (CODERABBIT_API_KEY, JIRA_URL, BROWSERSTACK_*, E2E_* etc.)
