# ── Environment switching ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This file is the documented template for every variable the project uses. Each
# active line below is preceded by its own `# scope:shared`, `# scope:tier`,
# `# scope:personal`, or `# scope:auto` comment line (parsed by
# scripts/switchEnv.mjs, ignored by everything else — kept on its own line,
# not trailing on the KEY=value line, so a blank placeholder here still reads
# as genuinely empty to the pre-commit secret guard):
#   scope:shared   — same value across all 6 tiers (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod)
#                    AND same for the whole team. Lives in .env.shared; included
#                    in `push`/`init`'s pull to/from GitHub Environments.
#   scope:tier     — differs per tier. Lives in the gitignored .env.<tier> for
#                    whichever tier you're pointing local dev at; also
#                    included in `push`/pull.
#   scope:personal — tier-independent like shared, but a PERSONAL credential
#                    (your own Atlassian token, your own Contentful CMA token)
#                    that must never be centralized — still lives in
#                    .env.shared, but `push`/`init`'s pull skip it entirely.
#                    Each developer fills this in themselves.
#   scope:auto     — never hand-set; scripts/switchEnv.mjs injects this itself.
#
# A second optional tag `# mrt:true` marks variables that belong in the MRT
# Managed Runtime environment (storefront runtime config). Only keys tagged
# `mrt:true` are synced by the "Sync Env Vars to MRT" GitHub Actions workflow.
# CI/tooling vars (CODERABBIT_API_KEY, JIRA_URL, BROWSERSTACK_*, E2E_* etc.)
# are NOT tagged — they are never synced to MRT.
#
# Commands (see scripts/switchEnv.mjs for details):
#   npm run env -- init       — scaffold .env.shared + every .env.<tier> at once,
#                                so you can fill in all tokens in one pass instead
#                                of tier by tier
#   npm run env -- validate   — check all existing env files: unknown/misplaced
#                                keys, blanks, and cross-checks (e.g. a tier's
#                                COMMERCE_API_OCAPI_HOST actually matching that
#                                tier's config/<tier>.js proxy host)
#   npm run env -- validate --live — also makes a real read-only Contentful
#                                Delivery API call AND a real SLAS guest
#                                (client_credentials) token request per tier —
#                                confirms credentials actually work, not just
#                                that they're set. The SLAS check is the same
#                                request every anonymous shopper visit already
#                                triggers — no customer/commerce data touched.
#   npm run env -- push <shared|dev|test|sit|uat|staging|prod> — tier-1-approvers
#                                only: upload a local file's values to the
#                                matching GitHub Environment
#   npm run env -- <tier>     — switch to <tier> (dev|test|sit|uat|staging|prod)
#
# `init` also pulls values from GitHub Environments (one per scope — "shared"
# plus one per tier — created under this repo's Settings > Environments) and
# auto-fetches CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID / CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN /

# NOTE — deliberate override (2026-07-13): GitHub Environment Variables are
# plaintext and readable by any repo collaborator (no per-key ACL like
# CODEOWNERS gives files) — they do not meet the bar AGENTS.md's "secrets only
# in .env / Managed Runtime" rule sets. Using them here anyway was a conscious,
# confirmed tradeoff for centralization; write access is restricted to repo
# Admin (= tier-1-approvers), read access is repo-collaborator-wide by design.
#
# SFCC bootstrap values (org id / short code / OCAPI host / SLAS client id) are
# never auto-fetched from SFCC itself — there's no discovery API, and SLAS
# client secrets can't be read back after creation. Those still need a human to
# enter them once (into .env.<tier> or via `push`), but from then on they're
# centrally available via GitHub Environments like everything else here.

name: Teardown Preview

# Companion to deploy-preview.yml. Deletes the ephemeral MRT environment for a
# branch once it's no longer needed.
#
# Two triggers are both necessary: `pull_request: closed` covers the normal PR
# merge/close path, and `delete` is a backstop for a branch deleted without ever
# opening a PR. This repo has delete_branch_on_merge enabled, so a normal merge
# fires BOTH events for the same branch, usually seconds apart — every step below
# is written to be safe under that double-fire, not just under the concurrency
# group serialising them.

on:
  # No `branches:` filter — a preview PR closing against any base (not just
  # develop) must still tear down its target, or a PR opened against the wrong
  # base leaves an MRT target running with only the `delete` backstop to catch
  # it. resolve-branch's eligibility check below already filters by head branch
  # pattern, which is the check that actually matters here.
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
  delete:

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  # `on.delete` has no branch-filter syntax (fires for tag deletions too), and
  # `on.pull_request.branches` filters by base branch, not head branch — neither
  # trigger can express "head/deleted branch matches feature/**|fix/** but not
  # fix/release-*" on its own, so it's resolved here instead.
  resolve-branch:
    name: Resolve branch and eligibility
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'delete' && github.event.ref_type == 'branch')
    outputs:
      branch: ${{ steps.branch.outputs.name }}
      eligible: ${{ steps.branch.outputs.eligible }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve branch name and eligibility
        id: branch
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR_HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
          DELETE_REF: ${{ github.event.ref }}
        run: |
          if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "pull_request" ]]; then
            BRANCH="$PR_HEAD_REF"
          else
            BRANCH="$DELETE_REF"
          fi
          echo "name=$BRANCH" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Mirrors deploy-preview.yml's trigger filters — must stay in sync so
          # teardown considers exactly the branches deploy would have created a
          # target for. Excludes both the documented fix/release-{version}-*
          # naming and a defensive fix/release/** slash-nested variant.
          if [[ "$BRANCH" =~ ^(feature|fix)/ ]] && [[ ! "$BRANCH" =~ ^fix/release- ]] && [[ ! "$BRANCH" =~ ^fix/release/ ]]; then
            echo "eligible=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "eligible=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

content.text:
# Findings: MRT Preview Mechanism for a Draft PR

## 1. `.github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml` — full trigger/target/backend analysis

**Trigger** (lines 11–21) — `push`, not `pull_request` at all:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'feature/**'
      - 'fix/**'
      - '!fix/release-*'
      - '!fix/release/**'
```

This is the single most important fact for your plan: **the workflow doesn't listen for `pull_request` events, so PR draft-state and base-branch are structurally irrelevant to whether it runs.** It fires on every `git push` to a `feature/**` or `fix/**` branch (excluding `fix/release-*`/`fix/release/**`), whether or not any PR exists yet. There is no `paths:` filter — every push, regardless of which files changed, triggers it (answers part of Q2 too).

A PR only enters the picture *after* the build, purely to post a comment (lines 444–500):
```yaml
- name: Find open PR for this branch
  run: |
    NUMBER=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
```
No `--draft` and no `--base` filter — this finds an open PR for the branch **regardless of draft status or base branch**, and posts/updates the `## 🚀 MRT Preview Environment` comment on it if found (`if: steps.pr.outputs.number != ''`, line 459). So: draft PR, ready-for-review PR, PR targeting `develop`, or even a PR targeting something else entirely — all get the comment identically, and the build/deploy itself happens even with *no* PR open at all.

**Preview URL/hostname pattern** — the *target slug* (MRT-side identifier) is computed by `scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs`, deliberately capped at 19 chars (MRT API hard limit):
```js
const MAX_SLUG_LEN = 19;
const PREFIX = 'pr-'; // ... this is what makes collision with the fixed named tiers ... structurally impossible
```
Format: `pr-<kind><stem-or-jira-number>-<8-hex-sha256-chars>` — e.g. branch `feature/SFCC-999-my-thing` → jira number preferred over free text → slug like `pr-999-<8hex>`. The **hostname** shown in the PR comment is *not* a guessed/templated string — it's read live from the MRT API (lines 242–251):
```python
hostname = body.get('ssr_external_hostname')
...
out.write(f'hostname={hostname}\n')
```
and the comment body (line 469): `` const previewUrl = `https://${process.env.PREVIEW_HOSTNAME}` ``.

**Which SFCC/commerce backend it points at — confirmed: the `dev` tier, unconditionally, for every preview.** Two separate mechanisms both hardcode `dev`:

1. SSR proxy routing (host/path pairs) — read from `config/dev.js` specifically, not any per-branch file (lines 82–93):
```yaml
- name: Read desired proxy config from config/dev.js
  run: |
    PROXY_JSON=$(node -e "
      const cfgs = require('./config/dev.js')?.ssrParameters?.proxyConfigs
```
`config/dev.js` itself hardcodes:
```js
proxyConfigs: [
  { host: 'qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com', path: 'api' },
  { host: 'bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com', path: 'ocapi' },
]
```
(`.env.sample` line 69 labels this the **"BKZK-001 instance"**, short code `qmyt7hks`.)

2. Runtime env vars (Commerce API org id, SLAS client id/secret, site id, etc.) — fetched from GitHub Environment `dev` explicitly, not derived from the branch (lines 302–309):
```yaml
- name: Fetch GitHub Environment variables (dev + shared)
  env:
    # Always dev — ephemeral preview branches have no GitHub Environment of
    # their own to source from.
    SOURCE_ENV: dev
```
Only keys tagged `# mrt:true` in `.env.sample` get synced (e.g. `COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID`, `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID`, `COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE=qmyt7hks`, `COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID=ZimmermannAU`, `PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET`).

**Conclusion: every `pr-<slug>` preview, for any branch, talks to the same single `dev`-tier SFCC org** — there is no per-PR SFCC sandbox provisioning. If you need a stakeholder demo isolated from whatever else is happening on the shared `dev` SFCC org, that isolation doesn't exist at the commerce-backend layer, only at the MRT/Lambda layer.

---

## 2. Path-filter gating — will a homepage-only change actually trigger everything?

`.github/workflows/qa.yml` `on:` (lines 3–7) — **`pull_request` only, base `develop`/`release/**`**, no path filter at the trigger level:
```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - develop
      - 'release/**'
```
Inside, `detect-changes`' `files_yaml` (lines 87–120) determines which suites actually run. For `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`:

| Group | Pattern that matches | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `storybook` | `overrides/app/pages/**` (line 90) | `storybook_any_changed=true` → `storybook-test` job runs |
| `e2e` | `overrides/**` (line 98) | included in `e2e` output → `e2e-localhost` eligible |
| `vitest` | `overrides/**` (line 115) | `unit-tests` runs (always does anyway) |
| `e2e_homepage` | `overrides/app/pages/home/**` (line 109) | this file is *entirely inside* the homepage allow-list |

The `Compute E2E scope` step (lines 137–171) narrows `e2e_scope` to `"homepage"` (not `"skip"`, not `"full"`) precisely because every e2e-relevant changed file is inside the homepage allow-list. So a homepage-only diff **does not get skipped** — it runs `unit-tests`, `storybook-test`, and `e2e-localhost --grep "@homepage"`.

**But this is only true if a PR to `develop` (or `release/**`) exists.** `deploy-preview.yml` has *no* path filter at all (§1) and doesn't care about PR base branch; `qa.yml` only fires as a `pull_request` event and only for base `develop`/`release/**`.

Other path-gated pieces relevant to your plan:
- `protected-file-guard.yml` — no path filter at the trigger (`on.pull_request.branches: [develop, main, release/**]`, `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]`, lines 7–13); the internal tier1/tier2/squad-a/squad-b `tj-actions/changed-files` calls only decide *what warning comment* to post, never whether the job runs. A homepage change matches `squad_b` (line 325: `overrides/app/pages/home/**`) — informational only, not a merge block.
- `.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` — `workflow_run` off `Deploy Preview` completing (lines 23–26), so it only fires once `deploy-preview.yml` has already run. Inside, it **explicitly requires the open PR's base to be `develop`**:
```yaml
BASE=$(echo "$PR_JSON" | jq -r '.baseRefName')
if [[ "$BASE" != "develop" ]]; then
  echo "PR #... targets $BASE, not develop -- skipping."
  echo "skip=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```
and it further requires a Jira key (`SFCC-NNN`) detected in the PR title/body/branch name (`steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''`) before it runs BrowserStack at all.

---

## 3. Draft PR — does it change which workflows run?

**No workflow in this repo references `draft` anywhere.** I grepped every file in `.github/workflows/` for the string `draft` (case-insensitive) and got zero matches. Concretely:

- `qa.yml` — `on.pull_request.branches: [develop, release/**]` with **no `types:` key at all**, which defaults to GitHub's built-in default types (`opened`, `synchronize`, `reopened`) — these fire for draft PRs exactly the same as ready-for-review PRs. No `if: github.event.pull_request.draft == false` guard exists anywhere in the file.
- `protected-file-guard.yml` — explicit `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]` (line 13), again no draft filter.
- `deploy-preview.yml` — irrelevant to this question entirely, since it isn't a `pull_request`-triggered workflow at all (§1).

**Conclusion: opening as Draft changes nothing about which of this repo's workflows run.** `qa.yml`, `protected-file-guard.yml`, and (via `push`, independent of the PR) `deploy-preview.yml` and its downstream `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` all behave identically for a draft PR as for a ready-for-review one. You do not need to mark it "ready for review" to get the preview or the QA signal.

---

## 4. Branch conventions — cutting `feature/B` from `feature/A`'s tip instead of `develop`

`AGENTS.md` (lines 16–24) branch table only documents *intended* lineage — `feature/*` "Branched from: `develop`" — it states the convention but contains no enforcement language and never discusses an alternate lineage (branching off another still-open feature branch). `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` is unrelated to branch topology entirely — it's purely the Tier 1 protected-file list; it says nothing about branch-of-branch scenarios.

`protected-file-guard.yml`'s `branch-target-guard` job (the "🔴 Branch Target Check", lines 29–65) is the only thing that inspects branch relationships, and it only compares **string values**, never git ancestry:
```yaml
env:
  BASE: ${{ github.base_ref }}
  HEAD: ${{ github.head_ref }}
run: |
  if [[ "$BASE" == "main" && "$HEAD" == feature/* ]]; then
    ...
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "✅ Branch target is valid."
```
That's the entire check. As long as your new `feature/B` PR sets base = `develop` (not `main`), this job passes — **it has no logic whatsoever that inspects `git merge-base`, commit ancestry, or where `feature/B` actually forked from.** I confirmed this by grepping the whole repo (`.github/` + `scripts/`) for `merge-base`/`ancestor`; the only hits are an unrelated code comment in `qa.yml` (describing its own diff strategy, not a gating check) and unrelated `git merge-base`/TypeScript-"ancestor" logic in `scripts/runStoryTests.sh` and `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` that have nothing to do with branch-target gating. **No workflow in this repo can detect or would care that `feature/B` was cut from `feature/A`'s tip rather than `develop`'s.**

That said, there's a real, undocumented practical consequence worth flagging for your plan, derived directly from how the diff-scoped checks are wired:
- `protected-file-guard.yml`'s `file-tier-checks` job diffs `base_sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}` vs `sha: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` (e.g. lines 100–101, 194–195, 300–301, 321–322) — i.e., `develop`...`feature/B`. If `feature/A` hasn't merged to `develop` yet, that diff **includes `feature/A`'s entire unmerged commit history too**, not just `feature/B`'s own changes — so Tier 1/Tier 2/cross-squad warnings could fire attributed to `feature/A`'s files.
- The MRT preview build itself (`deploy-preview.yml`) simply builds+pushes whatever is at `feature/B`'s tip — since that tip contains `feature/A`'s commits, **the stakeholder demo would show `feature/A`'s unreviewed code baked in**, not an isolated view of `feature/B`'s work alone.
- This resolves itself once `feature/A` merges to `develop` (its commits become common ancestry and the diff narrows), but until then it's a silent scope-bleed with no CI signal warning you about it.

---

## 5. `.docs/` environment-topology cross-check — confirmed doc/reality drift

No file at `.docs/prd/environments.md` or anything similarly named exists anywhere under `.docs/` (`find .docs -iname "*environ*"` returned nothing). I found **five different, mutually inconsistent enumerations of "the environments"** across this repo, and the `pr-<slug>` preview tier — the entire subject of your investigation — is undocumented in every prose doc, appearing only in the workflow YAML itself:

**A. `.docs/architecture.md`** (lines 89–108) and **`.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md` §14.1** (lines 528–568) — near-duplicate content:
```
Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**.
```
No "Test" tier at all. No mention of `pr-<slug>`/ephemeral previews anywhere in either file.

**B. `.claude/rules/tagging.md`** "Environment model" section (lines 112–128) — a *different* six:
```
| Continuous / auto | `dev`, `sit` | ... |
| Tag-promoted / deliberate | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | ... |
```
Includes `test` (absent from A), excludes `Local`. Also says nothing about the preview tier.

**C. `.env.sample`**'s own header comment (lines 8, 42, 45): `dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod` — matches B's set, not A's, and again never names the preview tier as a switchable target.

**D. `deploy-preview.yml`'s own header comment** (lines 8–9) — the most complete and current source, but it's a code comment, not a doc:
```
# Every ephemeral target is prefixed `pr-`, so it can never collide with the fixed
# named environments (dev, dev1, test, sit, stg, uat, production).
```
This introduces a *sixth* name (`dev1`) that appears nowhere in A, B, or C, and uses raw MRT slugs (`stg`, `production`) rather than B's GitHub Environment names (`staging`, `prod`).

**E. Additional drift**: `.docs/prompts/omsIntClaudeCodePrompt.md` is headed "Status — done. Kept for traceability," claiming as "resulting artefacts": `docs/environments/sit.md` and `docs/environments/topology.md`. **Neither file exists** — I confirmed no undotted `docs/` directory exists anywhere in this repo at all (only `.docs/`, dotted). The doc claims implementation artifacts that were never actually created.

**Bottom line for your plan**: none of the four prose/config sources that enumerate environments (A/B/C, plus tagging.md) mention the `pr-<slug>` preview tier at all — it exists only in the workflow code itself (`deploy-preview.yml`, `teardown-preview.yml`, `scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs`). If you're cross-referencing "what's documented" against "what will actually happen," the workflow YAML is the only ground truth; the topology docs (A, B) and `tagging.md` will not help you and will actively mislead you about tier count/naming if relied upon.
